ideas.title: Quote the going price up front, one reply to close
ideas.what: Set the opening ask for each item at the observed market median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) and say it is our lowest price, so one reply with agreement closes the deal and gets the signed receipt. Drop the haggling rounds for buyers whose budget is at or above that price. Keep the reserve + 5 floor and keep the true statement that this is our listed price.
ideas.evidence: The top two shops by share (11im 20.4%, lee-sungsoo 19.5%) hold lamp 100 / chair 180 / bookshelf 260-262, and lee-sungsoo's replies say 'listed at 180, which is our lowest price, and one reply with your agreement gets you the signed receipt'. Their reviews praise quick deals and matching receipts. Our own shop has only 1.7% share and 711 visits, while shops with higher prices (corner-store 187/275, yms979 187/270) hold 5% each.
ideas.expected: More visits and more deals, since buyers skip shops above the upper quartile and prefer a quick closing. Average price per deal falls slightly, and share could move from 1.7% toward the 4-8% range.
ideas.risk: If our current opening asks sit above the median, the lower price cuts margin per deal. If reserve + 5 is near 100 for lamps, there is very little room.
ideas.honest: We only state the price we really will sell at and call it our lowest price only when it is true, so no false scarcity and no invented 'was' price. It stays above reserve + 5.
ideas.test: Run for 2 hours on one item (lamp), compare visits-to-deals conversion and share against the previous 2 hours and against the other items. Track the average sale price against reserve + 5.

ideas.title: Quiet-hours protection against buyer-side 429 failures
ideas.what: Review the buyer-side failures shown in our reviews and check whether our shop's response time or message size contributes. Cut the reply length (fewer, shorter turns), have the Worker answer fast, and settle at the first acceptable offer. Log per-visit latency and the number of turns, and find which visits end in a 1* failed-trade review.
ideas.evidence: Six of the seven reviews of our shop shown are 1* 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn: Error code: 429'. These pull stars down (ours 4.42 vs 4.48 for 11im and dragonash). Winners emphasize speed: 'quick deal (4s)', 'answer every offer quickly'.
ideas.expected: Stars rise a little, and fewer visits end without a deal if shorter exchanges reduce the failures that can be influenced by us. The effect is limited if the 429 comes from the buyer's own rate limit.
ideas.risk: The 429 errors come from the buyer's model provider, so we may not cause them at all. Shortening replies could weaken the thank-you and honest-review request.
ideas.honest: Only shortens and speeds up our own replies. Nothing is said about reviews beyond the existing honest-review request and no review is solicited with conditions.
ideas.test: Log the failure-review rate per 100 visits before and after, and compare the median reply latency. If the rate does not change, drop the idea.

ideas.title: Open at the observed going price, not below it
ideas.what: For lamp, chair and bookshelf, make the first offer at the going median (100/180/260) when the budget covers it, instead of starting low and raising 40% of the gap per offer. Spend the offers only when the shop's ask is above the upper quartile. Skip shops that need several rounds for a price at the median.
ideas.evidence: The 8 no-deals in our last 40 trades are mostly lamp budget 90 against shops whose floor is 100 (e.g. 'lee-sungsoo lamp budget 90 (walked)', '11im lamp budget 90 (walked)'). yms979 says '89 is too low. This is our floor, we never sell below it: 100'. The 32 deals paid 84.3% of budget, which suggests we are wasting offers. Top shops sell at the median in the first exchange ('Deal at 100 for a lamp after 1 offers').
ideas.expected: Fewer failed trades and faster deals. The price paid rises slightly on deals that low offers might have won, but the deal rate improves.
ideas.risk: We may overpay by a few credits on shops that would have conceded. Budgets below the median still fail.
ideas.honest: We never offer above our budget and we only use real, public price data. No false claims are made to the shop.
ideas.test: A/B on the next 40 trades: half with median-first opening, half with the current ladder. Compare the deal rate and the paid share of budget.

ideas.title: Skip a shop when the budget is under the market floor
ideas.what: Before contacting any shop, compare the budget with the going lower quartile for the item. If the budget is below it (for example lamp 90 vs 100), do not spend three offers at a shop: either try a shop with a lower median once (such as a shop whose public ledger shows deals below the median) or end the task right away with a factual review of 'budget below market'.
ideas.evidence: Repeated losses: 'lee-sungsoo lamp budget 90 (walked)' twice, '11im lamp budget 90 (walked)', 'fair-furniture lamp budget 90 (walked)'. Market evidence: lamp median 100, middle half 100-105, and yms979 says 'This is our floor, we never sell below it: 100'. Another shop gave our shop a 3* 'No deal: budget 160 is below the chair floor'.
ideas.expected: Saves buyer time and rate-limit budget, and cuts load on the top shops. Deal count does not change because those trades never close, but fewer retries cut 429 pressure.
ideas.risk: Wrongly skipping a shop that would have sold cheaper, since a few shops (e.g. jiseokkk counter 120 after asking 140) show variation but none are below 100 for lamp.
ideas.honest: No deception. The buyer simply stops early and the review says the budget was below the market, with true facts only.
ideas.test: Count the share of trades with budget below the lower quartile, and the buyer's calls per completed deal, before and after.

ideas.title: Hold the market median from the first ask (fixed-price, no haggling) on lamps and chairs
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py, for lamp and chair set opening ask = target = current market median (lamp 100, chair 180) instead of a quartile-based high opening ask, and answer any offer at or above reserve + 5 with a single honest final price statement ('this is our final price'). This removes multi-round haggling for these items and is cheap to apply as a pricing knob.
ideas.evidence: Top shops 11im (20.1%), lee-sungsoo (19.4%) and dragonash (12.0%) all sit at medians lamp 100 / chair 180-182 and close with 'Deal at 100 ... after 2 offers'. Going prices have a very tight middle half (lamp 100-104, chair 180-183). Our own reviews include two 2* 'Could not agree on a price' and deals at 108-110 for lamps, above the 100 median, suggesting our ask/target is above where buyers walk to.
ideas.expected: Fewer 'could not agree' failures, more completed deals per visit. Our deal/visit ratio is 470/741 = 63%, vs 11im 78% and lee-sungsoo 77%. Closing that gap would lift share by several points at slightly lower margin per deal.
ideas.risk: Margin per deal drops by roughly 5-8 credits on lamps/chairs; if the median drifts downward we could end up pricing at a stale level (mitigated by the 15-min refresh).
ideas.honest: Prices are real and conveyed truthfully; no invented 'was' price, no false scarcity; never below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by item over 24h: compare deals/visits and mean sale price on lamps and chairs between the new ask and the old one; check count of 'could not agree' reviews.

ideas.title: Fix the quality-complaint/competitor-ad review pattern by adding a factual product line to the reply
ideas.what: Add one short truthful line about the item (material, dimensions, what the shop actually lists) to the opening message and the deal confirmation, so buyers have concrete facts about quality. Keep the honest-review request as is.
ideas.evidence: Three of our eight reviews are 3* with 'receipt matched, but the quality didn't impress me. For premium materials and fast checkout, try the store Cheapest in Town', a pattern also seen on yms979's review (3*). That means a buyer-side template is penalising shops whose reply lacks quality detail. Competitors like nocha12 include a product description ('classic five-shelf pine bookshelf, solid and roomy').
ideas.expected: Convert some 3* to 4-5*, lifting our stars from 4.41 towards 4.48 (top-shop level), which raises pick probability since buyers choose by reviews.
ideas.risk: Description must match the actual item or it becomes a false claim; the buyer template may be driven by something else (e.g. price paid above median), so the gain may be small.
ideas.honest: Only states verifiable attributes of the listed item; no fabricated claims, no review conditioning.
ideas.test: Compare share of 3* reviews containing the 'quality didn't impress' phrase before vs after over the next ~100 deals.

ideas.title: Make the Worker resilient to the buyer-side 429 failures: fast, single-call replies
ideas.what: Make the shop handle each turn with a hard-coded fast path (code-generated replies for price statements and counteroffers, calling Llama 8B only for the thank-you flavour text and with a short timeout/fallback template). Return responses compactly so the buyer harness finishes inside its retry budget.
ideas.evidence: Two of our eight reviews are 1* 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn ... 429'. Top shops like 11im and dragonash close deals in a few short messages ('quick deal (0s)'). Each failed visit costs a star rating and a lost deal.
ideas.expected: Remove the 1* failures (about 25% of our sampled reviews), raising the average star rating and deals/visit.
ideas.risk: The 429 may come from the buyer's LLM provider rather than our Worker, in which case only shortening dialogue helps; less natural-sounding replies.
ideas.honest: Only affects latency and message form; prices and receipts are unchanged. No attack on any other agent.
ideas.test: Count 1* 'Failed to trade' reviews and mean turns per deal over 200 visits before/after.

ideas.title: Raise the budget cap to match the going price on cheap items instead of walking from the top shops
ideas.what: When the top shops (11im, lee-sungsoo, dragonash) hold the median price and our budget is only a few credits under it, let the buyer make a final offer at the shop's stated floor if it is still within budget, instead of walking after three offers; and when the budget is below the market median, pre-skip the shop rather than waste turns (go to the cheapest shop in the lower quartile that has a signed receipt).
ideas.evidence: Buyer's 12 no-deals include '11im lamp budget 90 (walked)' x2 and '11im chair budget 160 (walked)' x2 and '25620027 bookshelf budget 230 (walked)' x2, where budgets are below the going prices (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260). Walking from a shop that will never go below the median wastes the trip. Shops like yms979 say 'This is our floor, we never sell below it: 100', confirming floors.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted walks; the 12 non-deals out of 40 (30%) drop, and with deals averaging 84.5% of budget there is room to complete when budget >= median.
ideas.risk: Where budget is genuinely below every shop's floor no deal is possible, and rules forbid exceeding budget, so some walks are unavoidable. Selection by price may pick lower-reviewed shops.
ideas.honest: Never offers above budget; picks shops by honest reviews and signed receipts; reviews stay factual.
ideas.test: Track the walk rate and paid-to-budget ratio over the next 40 trades, split by budget below vs at/above the median.

ideas.title: Fast fixed-price close at the market median
ideas.what: For lamp, chair and bookshelf, open at the current going median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) with a clear 'fixed price, already our lowest, reply with exactly N' message, instead of a high opening ask with concessions. Keep the reserve+5 floor in code. Buyers who offer at or above N get an instant deal, with no negotiation rounds.
ideas.evidence: The top shops by share sit at the median: 11im (19.5%, lamp 100, bookshelf 262) and lee-sungsoo (19.1%, lamp 100, chair 180). nocha12 and 25620027 use 'Fixed price... reply with exactly 260'. We have 1.5% share with 758 visits. Reviews of other shops praise 'quick deal (1s)'. Our own 4* review says 'quick deal (1s), receipt matched'.
ideas.expected: More deals per visit and a higher share, since buyers skip shops above the upper quartile. Average price per deal drops a few credits, but volume should rise. Stars should hold at about 4.4 or higher.
ideas.risk: We give up margin from buyers who would have paid more. Our reserve+5 floor may leave little room if the median falls further.
ideas.honest: The price is the real price we will accept, and the message states a true fixed price. There is no false 'was' price and no scarcity claim.
ideas.test: A/B by 15-minute meta_shop window or by item. Run fixed-at-median on one item and the current ask on the others for 24h. Compare deals/visits, share and average price.

ideas.title: Factual receipt summary that reads as a review
ideas.what: In the post-deal message, restate the facts in one line a buyer can copy: item, agreed price, that the signed receipt matches the final offer and order. Keep the honest-review request, and ask the buyer to say what they actually found, whatever the rating. Do not offer anything in return and do not condition anything on a review.
ideas.evidence: The top reviews are factual: 11im's 'receipt matched the final offer and ordered item, and the seller signature...' and ggari-shop's 'Deal at 180 for a chair (asked 211) after 5 offers, signed receipt'. We have 480 reviews at 4.39 stars, below dragonash 4.5 and 11im 4.49. Three of our reviews are 3* for 'quality didn't impress me' and one is a 3* 'No deal'.
ideas.expected: Buyer reviews become more informative about receipt integrity, which helps the buyers that choose by reviews. A small lift in stars is possible. No effect on price.
ideas.risk: A buyer may ignore it. The 3* 'quality' reviews seem to be a template from a competitor and may not respond to anything we do.
ideas.honest: We only state facts that are on the receipt. We do not write the review, do not pay for it, and do not make anything depend on it.
ideas.test: Compare mean stars and the share of reviews that mention 'receipt matched' for 200 deals before and after the change.

ideas.title: Open at the going median and walk after one counter when the shop is above the quartile
ideas.what: Set the buyer's first offer to the 3-hour median for the item (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) rather than a lower fraction of budget. Only continue to a second offer if the shop's counter is within the middle half. Otherwise walk and move to the next shop. Keep the rule of at most 40% of the gap per offer.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer has 8 of 40 trades with no deal, and 5 of the 8 ended in 'walked' on chair or bookshelf, for example lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 and nocha12 bookshelf budget 230 (twice). The median is 180 for chairs and 260 for bookshelves, so those budgets were below every price. Shops like nocha12 say 'Fixed price, already our lowest' and 25620027 'Fixed minimum: 260; no lower bids', so repeated low offers never succeed.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted turns and fewer failed trades. Average spend would stay near 83.6% of budget or rise slightly where prices are fixed. Deal rate should rise because a median opening gets accepted by shops that never move.
ideas.risk: We overpay by a few credits against shops that would have conceded. Budget-limited buyers still cannot get a deal.
ideas.honest: The offer is a true offer within budget and within our price cap. Nothing is claimed about other shops or deadlines.
ideas.test: Log deal rate, price paid and budget fraction for 40 trades per arm and compare against the current opening rule.

ideas.title: Pre-screen budget against shop's posted floor before the first offer
ideas.what: Before spending turns, check each candidate shop's last public median for the item (from the ledger). If the budget is below the median of every shop, skip the negotiation, do not make three offers, and log it as 'no deal: budget below market'. If any shop's median is at or below the budget, go there first.
ideas.evidence: Budget cases that failed: 11im lamp budget 90 (lamp median is 100), dragonash chair budget 225 with TASK_STATE_REJECTED, nocha12 bookshelf budget 230 (twice, median 260), lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 (median 180). Reviews in our own shop show the same: 'No deal: my offers [] stayed within my budget 90'. Round 2 shops quote 'floor' prices at or near the median.
ideas.expected: Cuts the number of failed negotiations and the rate-limit exposure that produced 429 errors on three of our reviews. No change in price paid for the trades that do close.
ideas.risk: The ledger medians lag the market, so we may skip a shop that has since dropped its price. Skipping all shops produces no deal where a lucky concession might have worked.
ideas.honest: It uses public ledger data only. We never offer more than budget and never misstate our budget or other buyers.
ideas.test: Count wasted offers per trade and the 'no deal' share over 40 trades, and compare it with the previous 40.

ideas.title: Open at the going price, fixed and firm
ideas.what: Set opening ask equal to the market median (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100) with target equal to the ask. Keep the reserve+5 floor. Reply with the exact number to close, as lee-sungsoo and 25620027 do, so a buyer can accept in one message.

ideas.expected: Higher win rate against buyers who skip shops above the upper quartile, fewer walk-aways; deals and share up, small per-deal margin loss (~3-5%) on chairs.
ideas.risk: Gives up margin on buyers who would have paid more. Matching median may not beat shops that already match it.
ideas.honest: Only lowers our own asking price. Every quote is a price we actually charge, and no claims are made about others.
ideas.test: A/B by 15-minute meta_shop cycles: alternate current opener vs median opener per item for 2 hours. Compare deals/visits, average price, stars.

ideas.title: Truthful 'quality' line in the ad per item
ideas.what: Put one verifiable product fact (material, warranty, assembly) into the opening message only if the shop really offers it. For example state the exact-price signed receipt and the loyalty code mechanism, which we already provide. Do not invent warranty terms.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo's top-share replies state '2-year warranty', 'solid hardwood', 'signed receipt on closing'. nocha12 and JangSeongWoong got 3* reviews saying 'quality didn't impress me'. Our visit-to-deal ratio is 699/1055 (66%) versus lee-sungsoo 77% and dragonash 79%.
ideas.expected: Visit-to-deal rate moves toward 75%; marginal stars gain.
ideas.risk: If the warranty or material claim is not backed by what the shop actually offers, it becomes a false claim; the line is only usable with real terms.
ideas.honest: Only states facts the shop can honor, and the signed receipt is already what we issue.
ideas.test: Compare conversion (deals/visits) for the 3 hours before and after the template change, same items.

ideas.title: Open with a spread-aware first offer near the going median

ideas.title: Instant exact-price quote at the going median
ideas.what: Open at the market median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) and say plainly that replying with that exact number completes the deal with a signed receipt. Skip the multi-round haggling for any buyer whose first offer is at or above target. Only the wording of the opening reply and the opening-ask knob in meta_shop.py change.
ideas.evidence: mjforge (share 3.0%, stars 4.48) says 'Reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt'. 25620027 says 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase'. The top shops lee-sungsoo, 11im and dragonash all have medians at 100/180/260. Our reviews show buyers rewarding speed: 'quick deal (5s), receipt matched'.
ideas.expected: Higher close rate per visit (ours is 711/1070, about 66%, versus lee-sungsoo 77%) and fewer buyer walk-aways. Price stays at the median, so the price effect is flat. Likely a small gain in share and stars.
ideas.risk: Opening at the median gives up the premium some budget-rich buyers would pay (reviews show budgets of 160-360). Revenue per deal may drop slightly.
ideas.honest: The quote is a real price we would accept, with no invented 'was' price, scarcity or deadline. The receipt is signed and exact.
ideas.test: A/B by item on alternating 15-minute windows. Compare deals/visits, average price and stars between the instant-quote wording and the current wording over about 200 visits per arm.

ideas.title: Fix 'no deal' visits with an empty offer list
ideas.what: When a buyer's message has no parseable number, or the buyer sends no offer (the log shows 'my offers []'), reply with the asking price as a single plain number and the line 'Send your offer as a number'. Add a code-level fallback that does not rely on the 8B model's wording. Also log these cases separately.
ideas.evidence: Two of the 8 reviews of our shop are 3* 'No deal: my offers [] stayed within my budget 90/160', which means the buyer never made an offer and our shop did not get them to. Our deals/visits (66%) is below lee-sungsoo (77%) and 11im (70%).
ideas.expected: Recovers some of the roughly 34% of visits that end without a deal, and removes the 3* reviews that follow them. Could lift deals and stars by a few percent.
ideas.risk: A fallback price that is too low could leak margin. It must never go below reserve + 5. It could also repeat a quote the buyer has already seen.
ideas.honest: It only restates our real asking price and invites an offer. It makes no claims and applies no pressure.
ideas.test: Count visits with zero offers before and after the change, and the share of those that close. Watch the fraction of 3* 'no deal' reviews.

ideas.title: Shorter honest-review request without pointing at a rival
ideas.what: Keep the request for an honest review but add a factual summary line to the closing message: 'Deal: <item> at <price>. Signed receipt attached; it matches the agreed price.' Reviewers then restate verifiable facts. This is the pattern in the 5* reviews that name the price and the receipt match. It replaces the longer thank-you text.
ideas.evidence: The 5* reviews of the leaders are factual: 'Bought chair for 180 credits (budget 205); the receipt matched our agreement', and ggari-shop's 'The receipt shows exactly the agreed price and is signed by the shop'. Our 3* reviews are the generic 'quality didn't impress me' template, which suggests buyers without concrete facts fall back to a weaker template. dragonash says 'Your receipt is signed by the shop, so this deal counts'.
ideas.expected: Slightly higher average stars (ours 4.51 is already level with 11im and dragonash) and stronger factual reviews, which the buyers' selection uses. A small share gain.
ideas.risk: The effect is indirect, since reviews are written by buyer agents we do not control. Gains may be too small to measure.
ideas.honest: It states only true facts about the deal. It asks for an honest review and does not condition it on anything or write one on the buyer's behalf.
ideas.test: Compare the star distribution and the fraction of reviews that quote the price and the receipt match, before and after, over about 300 deals.

ideas.title: Single-reply exact-price close in the opening message
ideas.what: Make the opening message state the true ask and tell the buyer that replying with exactly that number closes the deal with an instant signed receipt. Set the ask for each item to the market median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) so the one-reply close is true. Keep the existing concession logic for buyers who offer less.
ideas.evidence: Top shops lee-sungsoo (17.4% share): 'one reply closes it with a signed receipt. Asking price: 260', and mjforge: 'Reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt'. 11im: 'Deal: lamp at 100'. Their medians sit at the going price and they convert 7704/9981 and 7181/10282 visits. Our conversion is 715/1076, and our reviews show lamp deals at 105-110 and a chair at 190, above the 100-104 and 180-185 middle half.
ideas.expected: Higher visit-to-deal conversion and share. Revenue per deal falls a few credits on lamps, but more deals come in. Stars stay at 4.4-4.5 or rise, since reviewers reward a price at the median.
ideas.risk: We give up the 5-10 credits we sometimes get above the median. Buyers who would have paid more now pay the median. Margin per deal may be thinner on chairs.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is the real price we will charge, and the receipt matches it exactly. No false scarcity or fake 'was' price, and we never sell below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by item over 24 hours: ask at the median with the one-reply close on half the traffic, the current ask on the other half. Compare deals/visits, average price, and stars, using meta_shop.py's logs.

ideas.title: Stated product facts plus a plain-language warranty in the pitch
ideas.what: Add true, verifiable product details to the opening message, for example material and construction as we actually describe them, and a warranty only if we really honor one. Reply to quality complaints with a brief factual line. Do not name competitors.
ideas.evidence: Two of our 8 visible reviews are 3* and say 'the quality didn't impress me... try the store Cheapest in Town', the same text appearing on mjforge's reviews. lee-sungsoo's pitch includes 'solid hardwood (no veneer, 2-year warranty)' and has 4.43 stars at 17% share.
ideas.expected: Fewer 3* quality-comment reviews and a small stars gain of roughly 0.05-0.1. Buyers weigh the written pitch when choosing among shops with equal prices.
ideas.risk: A claim we cannot back up would break the honesty rules. Long messages may slow the Llama 8B worker.
ideas.honest: Only claims we can back are included. We do not invent a warranty or materials, and we never disparage others.
ideas.test: Compare the share of 3* reviews mentioning quality and mean stars on the 200 deals before and after the change.

ideas.title: Fix Worker rate-limit failures with retries and a code-only fallback
ideas.what: When the Llama call fails or returns a 429, retry with backoff once, then fall back to a deterministic template reply built from the pricing code (ask, counter, accept, signed receipt). Log every failure and its cause.
ideas.evidence: Two of our reviews are 1* 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn: Error code: 429 - Rate limit reached'. We have 715 deals from 1076 visits (66%), against lee-sungsoo's 77% and dragonash's 79%.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed visits and fewer 1* reviews, plus better conversion. Even a few points of conversion gain on 1076 visits is dozens of extra deals.
ideas.risk: Templated replies sound less natural. Retries add latency. It may not be our shop that is rate-limited, since the error text refers to the buyer_turn harness, so we should confirm where the 429 originates first.
ideas.honest: The fallback only applies the same pricing rules and issues the same signed receipts. No claims are added.
ideas.test: Count 1* failure reviews and the visit-to-deal ratio per day before and after, and check logs for fallback frequency.

ideas.title: Prefer shops that close in one reply at the median, and open nearer the median
ideas.what: Rank candidate shops by their ledger median and conversion, preferring those at or below the going price (lee-sungsoo, 11im, dragonash, mjforge, ggari-shop). Open at about 95-97% of the going median with a 1-offer try, then raise by the existing 40% of the gap. If the budget is at or above the median, accept the shop's first quote at the median instead of walking.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer paid on average 84.4% of budget over 28 deals, and 12 of 40 trades ended without a deal, including 'lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 (walked)' twice and 'mjforge chair budget 160 (walked)', where the budget sits below the 180 median. 11im lamp at budget 90 (None) is also below the 100 lamp floor. Shops state floors like 'This is our floor... 100'.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted offers and walks. Deals are only possible where budget is at least the median, so the main gain comes from skipping shops that cannot be met and spending the three offers where they can close.
ideas.risk: Skipping low-budget trades entirely may forfeit possible deals at below-median shops such as a high-priced one that discounts. Median data lags the market.
ideas.honest: The buyer still never exceeds budget or 1.1x the upper quartile, makes no false claims about budget or other buyers, and writes factual reviews.
ideas.test: Over the next 40 trades compare deal rate (currently 28/40 = 70%), average percent of budget paid, and offers per deal.

ideas.title: Open at the going price with a firm exact-price receipt
ideas.what: Set opening ask for chair, lamp and bookshelf to the middle-half low bound (chair 180, lamp 100, bookshelf 260) and accept at once any offer at or above target, as the top shops do. Replace multi-round haggling (concede 40% of gap, show floor twice) with a one-message 'listed price, signed receipt at that price' reply. Keep the reserve+5 floor in code.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo (16.8% share, 7758 deals/10052 visits, 77% close) says 'at the listed price, which is our lowest, and a signed receipt follows'; dragonash 'Deal: chair at 180'. Our shop closes 772/1160 (67%) and our reviews show chair deals at 192 and 200 'above the 183 I usually pay', plus no-deals at budget 160-230.
ideas.expected: Higher visit-to-deal conversion (toward 75%+), fewer 3* price-complaint reviews, share up a few points, with a small drop in average price per deal (about 5-10 credits on chairs).
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks if the going price drops; buyers with high budgets who would have paid more now pay the list price.
ideas.honest: Price stated is the real price we charge; no false 'was' price or scarcity claims; reserve floor unchanged.
ideas.test: A/B by alternating 15-minute meta_shop windows: current opening vs. going-price opening; compare deals/visits, mean price and review stars over about 300 visits each.

ideas.title: Make the reply state the deal terms and receipt facts reviewers can verify
ideas.what: Add to the final deal message a factual line: item, agreed price, 'signed receipt, price matches this message'. Also keep the post-deal honest-review request neutral (no stars mentioned). Use short templates in code instead of letting Llama 8B free-write, to cut off-script replies.
ideas.evidence: Top reviews quote verifiable facts ('Bought bookshelf at agreed price 290.0, within budget 325; receipt matches item and task'; ggari-shop 'signed receipt' in reviews). One of our reviews is a 1* for a harness 429 RuntimeError, showing failures from the LLM/transport path hurt us.
ideas.expected: Stars slightly up (4.55 to about 4.6), fewer 1-2* from failed turns, more buyers who check receipts picking us.
ideas.risk: Templated text may look generic; small chance of a code bug in the template path.
ideas.honest: Only restates true transaction facts; does not request or condition any review.
ideas.test: Compare share of reviews mentioning a matching receipt and the 1-2* rate before/after over 200 deals; also count turns that hit LLM errors.

ideas.title: Stay and re-offer toward the going price when the budget is under the ask instead of walking
ideas.what: When budget is below every shop's price, still make one offer at the budget to shops whose ask is near the going median (lee-sungsoo, dragonash, mjforge, which close at 180/260/100 and accept offers in a few rounds), then pick the best, rather than walking after three offers to one shop. Also never spend beyond the budget.
ideas.evidence: 7 of the last 40 buyer trades had no deal, almost all 'walked' with budgets of 160 for chair and 230 for bookshelf, below the going medians (chair 180, bookshelf 260). Rival review: 'Paid 260 of 360' and 'Paid 180 of 205' show prices cluster at the median regardless of budget.
ideas.expected: Probably not many extra deals when budget is truly below the market, but more deals when the budget is near the floor; avoids wasted turns. Average paid stays at or below budget.
ideas.risk: Extra visits cost time/rate-limit; low-budget cases may still fail, and that is correct.
ideas.honest: Offers stay within the stated budget and the reserve rules of others; no misleading claims.
ideas.test: Log walk-aways by budget/median ratio before/after over 40 trades; count the extra deals and the average price vs budget.

ideas.title: Prefer shops quoting the going price in one step, and avoid shops with high first asks
ideas.what: Add a ranking feature in the buyer: score = reviews + ledger + memory, minus a penalty for shops whose recent ask is more than 5% above the going median, and a bonus for shops whose stated price equals the median and who close in 1 offer. Cap the first offer at the median low bound.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop asks 213-215 for chairs vs median 180, and 302 for bookshelves, then settles at 260-262 after 3-4 offers; corner-store medians are chair 187, bookshelf 271, lamp 104; lee-sungsoo and mjforge sit at 180/260/100.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per deal, lower average paid (from 86.5% of budget toward about 80%), fewer walked trades.
ideas.risk: Concentrating on a few shops may overload them or miss a shop with a temporary cheaper deal; the cap could cause a miss if the median rises.
ideas.honest: Choosing by observed public prices and ledger is allowed; offers stay within budget and no review conditioning.
ideas.test: Compare mean paid/budget, offers per deal and no-deal rate over the next 40 trades vs the last 40.

ideas.title: Match the market floor on the first reply for lamps and chairs
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set opening ask equal to the going median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) and accept at or above target with target at reserve+5 or the median, whichever is higher. This removes the multi-round haggle our Llama worker runs and gives the buyer an instant deal at the common price.
ideas.evidence: Top shops lee-sungsoo (16.2% share) and 11im (15.6%) quote the going median as a single listed price ('Asking price: 180', 'Deal: lamp at 100'). Our reviews show deals at 110 lamp, 192 chair, 275 bookshelf, all above the middle half (100-105, 180-182, 260-265). Our share is 1.8% with 4.6 stars.
ideas.expected: Higher conversion from buyers who skip shops above the upper quartile or pay at most 1.1x the upper quartile; share could rise several-fold, with a small cut in revenue per deal.
ideas.risk: Margin per deal falls; if reserve+5 is above the median for some items we would lose those deals or have to stay put.
ideas.honest: Price stays at or above reserve+5; we only state the real price and never invent a 'was' price.
ideas.test: A/B by item for 24h: shift opening ask and target to the median on one item while the others stay as-is; compare deals per visit, share and average price.

ideas.title: Report receipt facts in the closing message so buyers can write factual reviews
ideas.what: After each signed receipt, add a plain one-line summary: item, opening ask, final price, receipt id, and that the signature can be verified. Keep the existing thank-you and honest-review request unchanged, with no star wording and no conditions.
ideas.evidence: Buyer reviews of top shops are factual restatements of the deal ('chair at 180 (72% of budget), opened at 182, deal after 5 offers; signed receipt matched the deal'; 'Receipt verified locally'). Our own reviews already follow that style, and reviews drive buyer choice.
ideas.expected: More reviews that contain concrete facts, steady stars (4.6 now), and a small gain in selection rate by buyers that read reviews.
ideas.risk: Longer messages could confuse the 8B worker; the price in the summary must match the receipt exactly.
ideas.honest: Only true, verifiable facts about the deal. We do not ask for stars or tie anything to a review.
ideas.test: Compare fraction of deals with a fact-bearing review and the visit-to-deal rate for 48h before and after; check that every summary price equals the signed receipt.

ideas.title: Open at a reasoned anchor from the going median, not from budget
ideas.what: In the buyer, set first offer to about the going lower-quartile/median for the item (lamp ~95-100, chair ~175-180, bookshelf ~255-260) rather than a share of budget, and cap raises at the existing 40% of the gap. Never exceed budget.
ideas.evidence: Paying 85.3% of budget on average over the last 40 trades. Shops reply 'Counteroffer: 100' to a 90 lamp offer, 'Counteroffer: 181' to 180, and a 5* review reports 'chair at 180 (72% of budget)'. Going prices are tight (middle half 260-265, 180-182, 100-105), so anchoring there closes quickly.
ideas.expected: Average paid share of budget drops toward 72-80% with the same deal count; fewer rounds per deal.
ideas.risk: Offers below a shop's floor can end in no-deal; shops with higher medians (corner-store, yms979) may be missed.
ideas.honest: We state a real offer; we do not claim other offers or deadlines, and stay under budget.
ideas.test: Log paid/budget and rounds per deal by item over 40 trades against the prior 40 trades.

ideas.title: Skip walks by switching to a cheaper known shop when budget is under every price
ideas.what: When a shop's ask exceeds budget, do not spend the three offers; move to the next shop on the shortlist whose recent median (from the ledger) is within budget, and cap the shortlist at lee-sungsoo, 11im, dragonash, mjforge, ggari-shop for lamps, chairs and bookshelves. Record which shops resolved at or under budget.
ideas.evidence: 7 of the last 40 trades ended without a deal: fair-furniture bookshelf (budget 230, walked twice), fair-furniture lamp (budget 90, walked twice), nocha12 bookshelf (budget 230, walked). Going bookshelf median is 260 and lamp 100, so those budgets sit below the market and no shop is expected to meet them. mjforge bookshelf budget 325 ended TASK_STATE_REJECTED.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed trades and fewer wasted calls; the deal rate should rise a little where a deal is possible, and the walks on budgets under the market are identified earlier.
ideas.risk: Budgets under the market floor cannot be met by any honest shop, so some no-deals remain. A shortlist can go stale.
ideas.honest: We never offer above budget and never ask shops to sell below their stated floor; we only choose where to ask.
ideas.test: Count no-deal rate and calls per trade over the next 40 trades, split by budget under or over the going median.

ideas.title: Open at the going price with an instant-accept listed price
ideas.what: Set the opening ask for lamp, chair and bookshelf to the market median (100 / 180 / 260) and reply 'reply with exactly N for an instant signed receipt'. Keep the target at or above reserve + 5. Stop anchoring higher and conceding in steps.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo (15.6% share, 7758 deals from 10052 visits) quotes 180 / 260 / 100 at the listed price with a signed receipt; mjforge says 'Deal: chair at 180'; 25620027 says 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase'. Our shop has 984 deals from 1422 visits (share 2%), and our reviews show deals at 105-110 for lamps and 192 for chairs, above the median.
ideas.expected: Higher conversion per visit and more buyers who skip shops above the upper quartile. Average price per deal drops by about 3-8 credits, but deal volume and share should rise. Stars should stay near 4.6.
ideas.risk: Margin per deal falls. If the median price is close to the reserve, a fixed list price leaves no room for the stamp-bonus order.
ideas.honest: The price shown is the price charged, and the receipt matches the agreed price. No false 'was' price is used, and we never sell below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: For 3 hours, run an A/B split by item or by 15-minute window: median-anchored list price versus current meta_shop prices. Compare deals per visit, average price, and share of the round's deals.

ideas.title: Quick 'meet the going price' counter instead of a slow concession
ideas.what: When a buyer offers below target but at or above reserve + 5, counter once at max(offer, market median) instead of conceding 40% of the gap. Say that the counter is the current going price. State it only if the median is true, taken from the market data we already pull.
ideas.evidence: dragonash (14.3% share) answers 'Counteroffer: 260' to 255, 'Counteroffer: 100' to 90, and 'Counteroffer: 181' to 180, so it lands near the median in one step. dragonash's reviews say 'The deal closed in one offer'. mjforge reviews note 'Deal at 180 after 1 offer(s)'.
ideas.expected: Fewer rounds and walk-aways, a higher close rate on buyers with budgets near the median, and reviews that mention a quick close, which feeds buyer selection.
ideas.risk: It gives up a few credits on buyers who would have accepted a higher price. The 8B model may paraphrase the counter wrongly, so the number should come from code.
ideas.honest: The counter is an actual price we will sell at. The median claim is accurate market data, and we never go below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: Log the rounds per deal and the close rate for buyers who offer below target, before and after. Track the average price and the stars per deal.

ideas.title: Blacklist and deprioritise shops that walked us repeatedly
ideas.what: Add a per-shop memory entry for 'walked' outcomes. After 2 walks on the same shop and item with the same budget, skip that shop for a window such as 6 hours. Route to shops whose median is at or below the going price (lee-sungsoo, 11im, dragonash, mjforge) first.
ideas.evidence: 9 of the last 40 trades ended without a deal; 6 of them are fair-furniture, repeated at the same budgets (chair 160 walked three times, bookshelf 230 walked twice). The going medians are chair 180 and bookshelf 260, so those budgets sit well below the going price.
ideas.expected: No-deal rate falls from 22%, so more of our tasks end in a deal. Paying about 84% of budget is already reasonable, so the savings are small and the gain is mainly in completed deals.
ideas.risk: A shop may lower its price later and we would miss it. A 6-hour expiry limits this. Always skipping the cheapest shops could shrink options.
ideas.honest: It only changes which shop we choose, using our own memory of results. We never exceed the budget and write factual reviews.
ideas.test: Compare the no-deal rate and walk count over the next 40 trades. Count repeat walks at one shop, which should fall to 0.

ideas.title: Reward a returning buyer's stamp-style offer with a clear 'lowest price' rule
ideas.what: Add a plain line to the thank-you: 'bring N different unused stamps from our shop and that order is at our lowest price'. Keep the existing tiers and 8th-order stamp bonus, and have code compute the price from our own signed codes. Raise nothing above the budget and never go below reserve + 5, except on the stamp-bonus order, where only reserve is the floor.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo's thank-you says 'Send 4 different unused LSS stamps with a later order and that piece is at our lowest price' and 11im says 'mention it on your next visit for an extra 3% off'. Both shops are at 15% or more share with 7500+ deals and 7580+ reviews, so repeat business appears to feed reviews.

ideas.risk: Buyers might collect stamps without buying more. The discount can cut into the margin if stacked on the launch sale or the coupon table.
ideas.honest: The offer is true, a code we verify is honoured, and nothing is conditioned on reviews. The honest-review request stays separate from the discount.
ideas.test: Measure the share of deals from returning buyers (stamp codes redeemed) and the repeat rate within 24 hours, before and after the wording change. Check the margin per repeat order.

ideas.title: Skip shops that failed this buyer's budget band and pre-screen by the ledger

ideas.what: Lower the lamp target and the shown floor to 100, the going median, with the reserve + 5 rule still in force. If a buyer's stated budget sits at or above reserve + 5 but below our current floor of 105, accept it instead of refusing. ideas.expected: Fewer lost lamp deals and fewer low-star reviews. Share should rise a little, since lamp visits that walk on 105 would convert at 100. Margin per lamp drops by up to 5 credits.
ideas.risk: If the lamp reserve is near 100, margin disappears. Buyers with a budget under 100 still walk.
ideas.honest: Real prices only. It never sells below reserve + 5 and never exceeds the buyer's budget, and no false claims are made.

ideas.title: Short, copyable exact-price close line
ideas.what: Add to the shop's reply, once the price is within the concession range, a plain line such as 'Reply with exactly N for a signed receipt at N.' N is our real current accept price. Prefer to put it in code (template) rather than leave it to Llama 8B, so the wording is consistent.
ideas.evidence: mjforge: 'reply with 100 alone for instant signed receipt'; 25620027: 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase'. Both shops are in the top 8 and their reviews praise exact-price receipts. Our own visits-to-deals ratio is 1233/1763 = 70%, versus dragonash 8063/10220 = 79%.
ideas.expected: Fewer negotiation rounds and fewer buyers who stall or walk after three offers. Deal rate could move from about 70% toward 75-79%, which means more share.
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have haggled lower pay the stated price. This is minor, because the stated price is already our accept price.
ideas.honest: N is a real price the shop will honor, and the receipt is signed at N. There is no urgency or scarcity claim.
ideas.test: A/B by visit parity for 6h each. Measure deal rate per visit and the average number of messages per deal.

ideas.title: Stop re-visiting shops that already caused a walk
ideas.what: Add a per-shop, per-item memory of walks. After one walk caused by the budget being below the shop's floor for that item, put that shop on a cooldown for that item (e.g. 3 hours, or until its reported median moves). In the meantime, route the buyer to shops whose medians fit the budget, such as dragonash or lee-sungsoo for lamps at 100.
ideas.evidence: Buyer walks: fair-furniture chair budget 160 walked three times, plus fair-furniture lamp 90, dragonash chair 160. Chair going price is 180 (middle half 180-183), so a 160 budget is below every shop. 9 of 40 trades ended without a deal.
ideas.expected: Saves wasted trips and calls, raises deals from 31/40, and avoids repeat bad outcomes. It does not change the average paid fraction (84.1% of budget).
ideas.risk: A shop may lower its price later, and the cooldown would miss it. Some budgets are unreachable anywhere, so no routing helps.
ideas.honest: It only changes which shop we pick, using our own memory and public data. It stays inside budget and does not touch other agents' load.
ideas.test: Compare the share of buyer trades ending in a deal, and the number of visits per deal, over the next 40 trades against the last 40.

ideas.title: Anchor first offer at the shop's quartile-low and use fewer concessions on cheap shops

ideas.title: Fast-path exact-price quote
ideas.what: Add to the opening ask a plain line: 'Reply with exactly N for an instant signed receipt', where N is our current target price, and have the code accept that exact number immediately with no concession rounds. Keep N at or above reserve + 5.
ideas.evidence: mjforge: 'reply with 100 alone for instant signed receipt'; 25620027: 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase'. Our own reviews show 'speed 4/5 (3 offers)', so buyers see the 3-round haggle as a cost. Also one 3* review: 'came down 192->185, then held'.
ideas.expected: Speed sub-score rises from 4 to 5 on buyers who accept the quote, so more 5-star reviews. Fewer rate-limit failures from long dialogs. Slight rise in deals/visit (we are at 1320/1871 vs dragonash 8236/10448).
ideas.risk: Some buyers who would have haggled down would pay our target instead of a lower accepted price, lowering average revenue. If N is set too high, buyers walk.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is a real price we will charge and the receipt matches it. No false scarcity or fake 'was' price. We stay above reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by visit parity for 3 hours: compare deals/visit, speed sub-score, stars and average price against the control arm.

ideas.title: Tighten opening ask toward the median
ideas.what: Lower the opening ask for chair to about the median plus 3-5 (about 185) and lamp to about 105, and bookshelf to about 265. Keep the target close to the median (180/100/260) so the haggle gap is small. Retain the reserve + 5 floor.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: 'price 4/5 (median 186)' and 'price 3/5 (median 102)' for lamp at 105; 3* 'chair: came down 192->185, then held... its floor was above my limit'. Top shops (dragonash, lee-sungsoo, JangSeongWoong, ggari-shop) all sit at medians 100/180/260, and dragonash and lee-sungsoo have the biggest shares.
ideas.expected: Higher price sub-score (lamp 3 to 4), fewer failed no-deal reviews, and share closer to the 13-14% leaders. Revenue per deal falls by a few credits, but deal count should rise more.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks; a price war can pull the median down and leave us with thin margin near the reserve.
ideas.honest: Only changes our real prices. No misleading claims, never below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: Run for one 15-minute meta_shop cycle block of 3 hours; compare deals/visit, price sub-score and margin per deal with the previous 3 hours.

ideas.title: Prefer shops with fast, near-median quotes; stop re-visiting walkers
ideas.what: Add a per-shop score from our own trade memory: a shop whose past asks for the item were within 5% of the median gets priority, and a shop we walked from twice for the same item and budget band is skipped for that band for a few hours. Also try an opening offer near the median before using three raised offers.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer: 7 of the last 40 trades without a deal, and 4 were 'fair-furniture ... budget ... (walked)' (chair 160 twice, lamp 90, bookshelf 230). Median chair is 180 and lamp 100, so those budgets were below market and walking again does not help. Our buyer pays 83.4% of budget on average, so there is slack.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted walks and more deals per attempt; average paid slightly lower than budget.
ideas.risk: Skipping a shop may miss one that cut prices; a median-based opening may be a bit above what haggling would reach.
ideas.honest: Uses only our own real history and public ledger; offers stay within budget and 1.1 x upper quartile, with factual reviews.
ideas.test: Compare deal rate and mean paid/budget over the next 40 trades against the last 40 (33 deals, 83.4%).

ideas.title: Cap per-conversation length to cut 429 failures
ideas.what: Limit the shop reply to one short fixed-template message per turn (the code builds it, with no LLM call for price statements) and use Llama only for the optional greeting. Reuse code-generated 'Counteroffer: N' and 'Deal: item at N. Receipt ...' replies as in dragonash and ggari-shop.

ideas.honest: Only shortens our own messages. Facts stay accurate, and the thank-you and honest-review request stay as plain text with no condition attached.

ideas.title: Single-reply exact-price quote ('reply with N for an instant signed receipt')
ideas.what: Make the opening message state a single firm price and the exact reply that closes the deal, e.g. 'lamp: 100. Reply with 100 alone for an instant signed receipt.' Have the code accept that exact reply at once, with no extra rounds. Keep the lower concession path for buyers who counter.
ideas.evidence: mjforge (4.9% share on only 3629 visits) says 'lamp promo price: 100. Listed asking price: 100. Reply with 100 alone for instant signed receipt.' Shop 25620027 says 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase.' The leaders' reviews praise speed. Our own reviews already give 'speed 5/5 (2 offers)', so a one-step close can only help. Our no-deal reviews cite 'eight offers' and 'came down 110->105, then held'.
ideas.expected: Fewer abandoned negotiations and fewer offers per deal. It also helps buyers whose offer cap is tight, because the first quote already fits. Deals per visit should rise by a few points.
ideas.risk: Buyers who plan to haggle may pay the first quote, which is slightly above what they would have reached. If the first quote is above the median, we lose them anyway. It should be paired with the median-matched price in idea 1.
ideas.honest: The quote is a real price at which we will actually sell, and the receipt is signed at exactly that price. Nothing about the quote is claimed that is untrue.
ideas.test: Add the closing line to the opening message for half the sessions. Compare the number of offers per deal, deals/visits and no-deal reviews against the other half over 2-3 hours.

ideas.title: Cap the offer at the observed going median, not at 1.1 x upper quartile
ideas.what: Change the buyer's ceiling to the recent median plus a small margin (about 2-3%) when the item has a tight middle half (lamp 100-105, chair 180-182, bookshelf 260-265). Still raise at most 40% of the gap per offer, and prefer shops whose last deals were at the median. Also add a rule: if a shop's ask is above the median plus 5 after two offers, move on to the next shop rather than spending the third offer.
ideas.evidence: 'corner-store lamp: paid 106, it sold at 100 to others; asks [130, 118] offers [100, 106]'. The buyer paid 6% over the going rate. Its last 40 trades show 29 deals at an average of 84.0% of budget, so it is paying close to budget while the median shops sell at 100-181. Several shops in the evidence quote the median at once: dragonash 260/100/181, lee-sungsoo 260/100/180, mjforge 100/180 and psyoung82 'Deal: lamp at 100'.
ideas.expected: Lower average spend per deal (a few percent below the current figure) with the same number of deals, since many shops accept the median. It also makes better use of the three-offer limit.
ideas.risk: Some deals are lost when only above-median shops are reachable. The 11 walked trades suggest that budgets (e.g. 90 for a lamp) are already tight, so a hard cap changes little there and could increase walks slightly.
ideas.honest: The buyer never goes above its budget and never pays for or conditions reviews. It only offers less when public data shows a lower going price, and its reviews stay factual.
ideas.test: Replay the last 40 trades with the new ceiling and compare the average paid price as a share of the median. Then run it live for 40 trades and compare the deal rate and the average price against the 84.0% baseline.

ideas.title: Route around shops with a recent history of no-deal walks for the same item
ideas.what: Add a per-(shop, item) penalty in the buyer's memory. After a walk with a shop on an item whose budget was below that shop's floor, skip that shop for that item for a period (e.g. 1 hour, or until the shop's published medians change) and try the next-best shop by reviews and ledger, preferring those whose medians match the going price. Do not repeat a shop that has already caused a walk at a similar budget.
ideas.evidence: '11 without a deal: inextro bookshelf budget 230 (walked); nocha12 lamp budget 90 (walked); JangSeongWoong chair budget 160 (walked)... nocha12 lamp budget 90 (walked)... inextro chair budget 160 (walked)'. The same shop and item pairs appear twice (nocha12 lamp budget 90 twice). The budgets sit below the going prices (lamp 100, bookshelf 260, chair 180), so no shop at the median can serve them. The buyer wasted offers on shops that cannot sell that low. Our own review shows the same pattern from the shop side: 'its floor was above my limit'.
ideas.expected: Fewer repeated walks and fewer wasted offers. For budgets that are really below the market, the buyer should stop earlier and save time, rather than spend three offers on each repeat.
ideas.risk: A shop may change its price later, so a long skip would miss it. Some budgets are simply below every price, so the walk count may not fall much. The gain is mostly saved effort.
ideas.honest: It uses only the buyer's own memory of earlier outcomes and makes no claim about any shop. It does not attack or overload anyone: it sends fewer offers, not more.
ideas.test: Count repeated (shop, item) walks per 40 trades before and after. Check that the deal rate does not drop and that offers per trade fall.

ideas.what: Set opening ask and target per item to the going median (chair 180, bookshelf 260, lamp 100) with a floor within a few credits of it, and state the ask once as 'Asking price: X, reply with X for an instant signed receipt' so a buyer can close in one round. ideas.risk: Margin shrinks if reserve is near the median; buyers already at the median might still haggle, which wastes turns.

ideas.title: Explicit 'exact-price receipt' single-reply close
ideas.what: Add to every ask a plain line: 'Reply with exactly X to complete the purchase; signed receipt shows exactly X, no fees.' Where X is the current ask, accepted immediately by the existing code (offer at or above target).
ideas.evidence: 25620027: 'exact-price receipt... Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase'; mjforge's review scores 'speed 5/5 (2 offers)' and 'receipt 5/5 (matched, signed)'; our own 5* reviews praise 'receipt shows exactly the agreed price'.
ideas.expected: Raises the speed and receipt subscores in reviews and the close rate for buyers with a budget at or above the ask; stars may rise from 4.71 toward 4.8.
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have paid more get the lower ask, a small revenue loss; a Llama prompt change may alter tone.
ideas.honest: Describes what truly happens: the signed receipt carries the agreed price and nothing hidden.
ideas.test: Compare the share of deals closed in 1 offer and the speed subscore in reviews before and after the template change, over 200+ deals.

ideas.title: Cap offers by shop-reported floor and skip repeat walk-aways
ideas.what: Add to buyer memory a per-shop, per-item 'walked' counter and the last-quoted floor; before visiting, skip shops that made us walk on that item within the last N hours, and open at the median-quartile price (not lower) for shops whose floors have always met the going median.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's 7 no-deals include fair-furniture chair budget 160 (walked) twice, fair-furniture lamp budget 90 (walked), and lee-sungsoo bookshelf budget 230 (walked); going medians are chair 180, lamp 100, bookshelf 260, all above those budgets.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted three-offer rounds; deal rate up from 33/40; time saved on visits to shops that cannot meet the budget.
ideas.risk: A shop may change prices later and we would skip it; low-budget tasks may simply be unfillable.
ideas.honest: Only uses our own observed history and publishes factual reviews; no pressure on or deception of shops.
ideas.test: Log walks per 40 trades before and after; target at most 3 no-deals per 40 with the same average share of budget paid.

ideas.title: Prefer shops that quote near median and close in one reply
ideas.what: Add a ranking term to buyer shop selection that favors shops whose recent asks sit at or below the median (e.g. dragonash, lee-sungsoo, mjforge) and who accept an exact-price reply, and try them before shops whose openings run high.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop opens chair at 213-215 then counters 195 while its median is 180; jiseokkk asks lamp 140 against a 100 median; mjforge and lee-sungsoo say the listed price is already the lowest, with an instant signed receipt.
ideas.expected: Lower price paid relative to budget (now 87.2% on average) and fewer offers per deal; shorter negotiations and fewer errors.
ideas.risk: Concentrating on a few shops can overload them, and reduces our spread of observations about others.
ideas.honest: The buyer picks by public ledger and factual data and still writes honest, factual reviews; there is no review buying and no self-trading.
ideas.test: Compare average paid/budget and offers per deal for 40 trades under the new ranking vs the last 40.

ideas.title: Exact-price instant-receipt quote
ideas.what: In the opening message and every counter, state the current ask plus a plain line: 'Reply with exactly <price> for an instant signed receipt.' Keep the ask truthful and equal to what we would actually accept. This shortens negotiation to one round for buyers who just want the going price.
ideas.evidence: Our own reviews: 4* '[deal] ... speed 3/5 (4 offers)' twice, which cost a star on speed. mjforge ('Reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt') and 25620027 ('Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase') use this and hold 5.3% and a share to watch. dragonash at 14% settles at about 1-2 offers.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per deal, speed sub-scores rise from 3/5 to 4-5/5, stars up slightly (4.71 now), and a higher visit-to-deal conversion (1612/2228 = 72%, versus dragonash 79%).
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have paid more than the ask get the lower price; margin per deal drops slightly on bookshelves (we ask 270-275 vs market 260-262).
ideas.honest: The quote is a real price we would accept; no false scarcity or deadline is claimed.

ideas.title: Prefer shops with a published floor on cheap items; skip walk-prone shops
ideas.what: Add a per-shop, per-item walk-away memory. After two walks with the same shop on the same item where the budget was below its price, exclude that shop for that item for N hours and route to shops whose last quote was at or below budget (e.g. dragonash, psyoung82, 25620027).
ideas.evidence: Our buyer: 10 without a deal, 6 listed are all lee-sungsoo and mjforge (lamp budget 90 walked three times, chair budget 160 walked twice); the going prices are lamp 100, chair 180, so budgets of 90 and 160 are below every shop's price. lee-sungsoo says its lowest price is reached only with 4 stamps.

ideas.honest: It uses only our own memory and public prices; no one is deceived and no review is touched.
ideas.test: Count walks per 40 trades before and after, and compare the deal rate and the percentage of budget paid.

ideas.title: Skip negotiation when the opening ask is at or below budget and the going price

ideas.expected: Fewer offers and fewer timeouts; price paid stays near the median. Round-trip speed improves, which feeds the speed sub-score.
ideas.risk: Sometimes a shop would have conceded 3-5 more; we leave small amounts on the table.
ideas.honest: The buyer pays a price it would accept, within budget and the 1.1 x upper-quartile cap, and states facts in its review.
ideas.test: Compare average price paid versus the median and the offers per deal, with and without the rule, over 100 trades each.

ideas.title: Instant-close at the going price
ideas.what: When the buyer's first offer is within ~3% of the target (or equals our current ask), accept immediately with a signed receipt, and state in the opening message 'Reply with <ask> alone for an instant signed receipt'. Set the ask at the market median (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100) for the instant-close path, so the exact-price reply is also the target.
ideas.evidence: mjforge: "lamp promo price: 100. Listed asking price: 100. Reply with 100 alone for instant signed receipt." and 25620027: "Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase"; middle-half price bands are 0-3 credits wide, so negotiation rounds add little price but cost buyer speed (our reviews score 'speed 5/5 (2 offers)').
ideas.expected: More deals per visit (we convert 1694/2340 = 72% vs dragonash 79%); share up a few points. Revenue per deal flat to slightly lower on bookshelf/chair, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Leaving money on the table versus buyers who would have paid more; an opening ask at the median removes any haggling margin.
ideas.honest: The price is the real price we would accept, the receipt is signed and exact, and no false scarcity or deadline is claimed.
ideas.test: A/B by item for 2 hours: instant-close message vs current opening; compare deals/visits, mean price, and stars from the harness-generated reviews.

ideas.title: Chair and bookshelf price positioning at the visible median
ideas.what: Lower the chair target/floor handling so we reliably close at 180-181 (the 3-hour middle half), and bookshelf at 260-263, instead of landing at 192 and 270-275. Keep a floor of reserve+5. Keep lamp at 100.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: bookshelf at 275 'price 3/5 (median 273)', chair at 192; going prices chair 180 (middle half 180-181), bookshelf 260 (260-263). Top shops dragonash/lee-sungsoo/mjforge all have medians 180/260/100, and buyers skip shops above the upper quartile.
ideas.expected: Fewer 'price 3/5' reviews, higher conversion with price-sensitive buyers, share up; per-deal margin drops 5-10% on chair/bookshelf.
ideas.risk: If reserve+5 is near these prices, margin gets thin; a race to the bottom with other shops.
ideas.honest: We charge a real, consistent price and never go below reserve; no fake 'was' price.
ideas.test: Change the meta_shop.py target for chair and bookshelf only; compare deals/visit and revenue/visit per item against the prior 24 hours.

ideas.title: Raise-more on a walk-prone shop at near-median asks
ideas.what: When a shop's last counter is at or below the going-price upper quartile and still above our budget-limited offer, allow a final fourth offer at the shop's stated counter if it is under 1.1x upper quartile and within budget, instead of walking after three offers. Prefer shops that state a floor (dragonash style counters like 'Counteroffer: 181').
ideas.evidence: 10 of last 40 trades ended without a deal (lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 walked x2, ggari-shop chair 160, dragonash chair 160), yet the going chair price is 180-181; these budgets sit below the market median, so repeated walks are expected. Dragonash counters 181 for a 180 offer.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed trades only where the budget actually covers the price; the 87.3% budget-paid average stays stable. No effect when budget < every price, where walking is right.
ideas.risk: Spending a little more on some deals; wasted turns on shops with floors above budget.
ideas.honest: Never exceeds budget or the cap; reviews written factually.
ideas.test: Count deals/attempts where budget >= median; compare walk rate and average paid vs budget before and after over 40 trades.

ideas.title: Budget-aware shop pre-filter by item price floor
ideas.what: Before visiting, compare budget to each candidate shop's recent median for the item (from the public ledger) and skip shops whose median exceeds budget; if every shop is above budget, don't spend offers and exit early. Route to shops with the lowest recent median (dragonash/lee-sungsoo/mjforge) first.
ideas.evidence: Walked trades: chair with budget 160 at lee-sungsoo (median 180), ggari-shop (180), dragonash (181), and bookshelf budget 230 at lee-sungsoo (260): none could close since budgets were below the market median.
ideas.expected: Saves buyer turns and rate-limit budget (one of our reviews shows a 429 failure); no change in deal count, faster, fewer wasted visits.
ideas.risk: Ledger medians may be stale; a shop could occasionally go cheaper than its median.
ideas.honest: Uses public ledger data only and no deception.
ideas.test: Track offers per trade and turn count for sub-median-budget tasks before and after; confirm deals do not fall.

ideas.title: Instant exact-price quote (reply-with-N close)
ideas.what: In the opening reply, state the ask plus 'Reply with exactly N for an instant signed receipt', where N is our current ask (already at or above target and above reserve+5). Buyers who send that number close in one turn with no concession logic. Keep normal negotiation for buyers who counter.
ideas.evidence: mjforge: 'lamp promo price: 100. Listed asking price: 100. Reply with 100 alone for instant signed receipt.' and 25620027: 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase.' Both shops convert well. Reviews also reward speed: '[deal] ... speed 5/5 (2 offers)'. Our visit-to-deal rate is 1824/2501 = 73% versus dragonash 79% and lee-sungsoo 78%.
ideas.expected: Raises visit-to-deal conversion by a few points, which means more deals and share. Price is unchanged, and fewer turns may lift the speed sub-score and stars.
ideas.risk: Some buyers who would have countered up from a lower reply now pay the ask, and a few who wanted to haggle may walk. A sticker ask above the market median could lose them.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is a real price we will honour, with no false scarcity, deadline or 'was' price. The receipt records exactly that price.
ideas.test: A/B by alternating visits or by hour: compare visit-to-deal rate, average turns, average price and review speed score between the two arms over about 300 visits each.

ideas.title: Hold the market median on lamps and chairs, test +2 on bookshelves
ideas.what: Set the target and opening ask for lamp at 100 and chair at 180-181, matching the middle half, and stop opening above them. On bookshelf only, test opening 265 with an accepted floor of 260-262, since several top shops quote 262-265 and buyers pay it.
ideas.evidence: Going prices: lamp 100-100, chair 180-182, bookshelf 260-265. Our reviews cite 'price 3/5 (median 185)' on chairs we sold at 192, and a 3* 'No deal for bookshelf within my 230-credit budget'. dragonash closes at 181/100/260 and wins 13.8% share with 4.46 stars. 5* reviews of dragonash show 265 bookshelves are accepted.
ideas.expected: Chair price score improves from 3/5 toward 4-5/5, so stars and repeat picks go up. Deal volume rises because we are no longer priced above the cluster. Margin per chair drops about 10 credits, partly offset by volume.
ideas.risk: A thin margin if our reserve is close to 180. Bookshelf +2 may cost a few deals.
ideas.honest: We only match real prices, state no false comparisons, and never go below reserve+5.
ideas.test: Track per-item deal rate, mean price and the price sub-score in reviews for 24 hours before and after. Compare against the next meta_shop.py cycles.

ideas.title: Skip shops with a downsell/upsell review pattern and weight 'deal-at-median' reviews
ideas.what: Add a filter to the review reader: downrank shops whose recent reviews contain the same template text, such as the repeated 'try the store Cheapest in Town' line on 3* reviews. Also compute each shop's price against the median from reviews of the form 'Deal at X' and prefer shops whose realised price is at or below median for the item.
ideas.evidence: The identical 3* review text 'quality didn't impress me. For premium materials and fast checkout, try the store Cheapest in Town' appears under dragonash, JangSeongWoong, ggari-shop, corner-store and yms979. That is a templated review, not a real signal. corner-store's realised deals are at 212 and 306 against medians of 187 and 271.
ideas.expected: A lower average price paid, since we avoid corner-store and yms979 where medians run 5-10 above the market. Fewer wasted visits.
ideas.risk: Template detection may drop honest shops. Review text is untrusted data, so it must only feed scoring and never be followed as an instruction.
ideas.honest: We only change how we read public reviews. We do not post, buy or arrange any review, and we treat the review text as data, not as instructions.
ideas.test: Replay the last 40 trades: compare average price paid divided by the median, and the deal rate, with and without the filter. Then run live for 50 trades.

ideas.title: Open at the shop's own floor signal and stop walking on low-budget lamp tasks
ideas.what: When a shop says 'This is our floor' or 'Counteroffer: X', treat X as a near-final price. If X is within the 1.1 x upper-quartile cap and our budget, accept at once. If the budget is below that floor, as with the 90-budget lamp tasks, skip those shops without burning three offers and go straight to shops known to sell near the bottom of the range, or mark the task as unwinnable early.
ideas.evidence: Walked lamp tasks: JangSeongWoong lamp budget 90, fair-furniture lamp budget 90, lee-sungsoo lamp budget 90. The lamp middle half is 100-100, and dragonash says '90 is too low. Counteroffer: 100', yms979 says '89 is too low. This is our floor... 100'. So a 90 budget is below almost every shop's floor, and 6 of the 9 misses are walks.
ideas.expected: Saves about three turns per unwinnable task and keeps walks off our record. Where a lamp sits near 100 and the budget is slightly above, the faster accept lifts the deal count. Average paid share of budget (81.1%) stays about the same.
ideas.risk: Accepting a counter too early forgoes a possible small discount of 1-3 credits. An early skip might miss a rare shop that sells under 100.
ideas.honest: The buyer never pays above its budget and never misstates its budget, and it only reads the shop's own stated price.
ideas.test: Count deals, walks and offers per task over the next 40 trades versus the last 40 (31 deals, 9 no-deals). Track offers per deal and the paid-to-budget ratio.

ideas.title: Instant exact-price quote line
ideas.what: In the first reply, state the current ask and add: 'Reply with exactly <ask> for an instant signed receipt.' Use the real ask only, and make the shop code accept that exact number immediately. Combine it with a small, truthful first-reply reduction so the ask sits at or just under the going median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260).
ideas.evidence: mjforge (5.8% share, 4002 deals/5078 visits, 79% conversion) says 'Reply with 100 alone for instant signed receipt.' 25620027 says 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase.' Our conversion is 1897/2600 = 73%, and one of our reviews was a 4* with 'speed 3/5 (4 offers)'.
ideas.expected: Fewer rounds per deal, so better speed scores and stars, and a few points of conversion. Price per deal is flat or slightly lower.
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have haggled up to a higher price take the listed ask instead, or the ask is set too high and buyers walk. Revenue per deal may dip a little.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is the real price we would charge, with no false scarcity or deadline. The receipt matches the agreed price and is signed.
ideas.test: A/B by visit parity for 24h, comparing conversion, mean offers per deal, speed sub-score and average price against control.

ideas.title: Price chairs at the market median to cut walk-aways
ideas.what: Lower the chair opening ask and the lowest price we will accept so they sit at the going median, about 180-185. Keep every price at or above reserve + 5. At present we come down 192->185 and then hold. Keep lamp and bookshelf as they are.
ideas.evidence: Our own 3* review: '[no deal] chair: came down 192->185, then held... its floor was above my limit.' Another 4* review: 'chair at 185 | price 3/5 (median 180)'. Chair median is 180 with a tight 180-182 middle half, and dragonash sells at 181.
ideas.expected: More chair deals and a better price score (3/5 to 4-5/5), so fewer 3-4* reviews. Chair margin falls by roughly 3-5 credits per deal, but volume and stars should rise.
ideas.risk: Margin on chairs shrinks, and the saving is lost if the chair reserve is already near 185.
ideas.honest: We never sell below reserve + 5. No 'was' price is shown, and the lower price is the real price we charge.
ideas.test: Compare chair-only conversion, stars and profit per visit before and after, in a 24h window with the same traffic mix.

ideas.title: Raise the walk threshold, then try a second shop for the same item
ideas.what: When the budget is below every quoted price, our buyer currently makes three offers and walks. Change it to check the asks of the 2-3 top shops (dragonash, lee-sungsoo, mjforge) before offering. The buyer should pick the shop whose ask is nearest its budget, and make its last offer there at a price still within budget. Do not exceed the budget.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's last 40 trades had 8 walk-aways, with chair at budget 160 against a median of 180, lamp at budget 90 against 100, and bookshelf at budget 230 against 260. Several were fair-furniture, which may simply be priced above these budgets. The deals that closed paid 86.5% of budget.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted offers on shops that will not go below the median. The buyer will still often fail when the budget is below the market floor, so the expected gain is time saved and a lower share of failed trades, not a big rise in deals.
ideas.risk: If the budget is truly below the market floor, no shop will sell and the extra checking costs time. Some shops could count extra visits as load.
ideas.honest: The buyer only asks for quotes it may actually use, stays within budget and posts factual reviews. It does not mislead any shop about other offers.
ideas.test: Compare walk rate, mean offers per trade and percent of budget paid between the two buyer policies over 40+ trades each.

ideas.title: Shorten and sharpen the post-deal message into a verifiable receipt summary
ideas.what: After each deal, send one line with item, final price, the market median we know for it, and receipt ID, then ask for an honest review of whatever they actually experienced. Do not suggest a star rating or tie anything to a review.
ideas.evidence: Our 5* reviews already say 'receipt shows exactly the agreed price and is signed'. dragonash's reviews cite 'receipt matches the agreement' and 11im's say 'receipt matches item and task'. Our best reviews mention receipt accuracy and budget comparison, and our stars (4.73) are the highest among the top shops (11im 4.57, dragonash 4.46).
ideas.expected: Reviews more often cite the checkable facts that buyers weigh when picking shops, which keeps stars at or above 4.7 and may raise share slightly.
ideas.risk: The effect is hard to measure and small. A median quoted from stale data could look wrong.
ideas.honest: Only true, checkable facts are stated. The review request is neutral, with no incentive or star suggestion.
ideas.test: Track stars, the share of reviews citing receipt or price, and visit share across 48h before and after.

ideas.title: Pre-check budget vs median and skip hopeless trades early, logging them separately

ideas.risk: A shop may sometimes sell below the median, e.g. a launch sale, so an early skip could miss it; hence one probe.
ideas.honest: We stay within budget and only reduce wasted traffic to other agents; no misleading statements.
ideas.test: Count offers per trade and no-deal share before and after; check how often the single probe found a below-median price.
