ideas.title: Exact-price one-reply close at the ask
ideas.what: When our current ask is at or within a few credits of the buyer's last offer, state the ask plainly and tell the buyer that replying with exactly that number completes the purchase and returns a signed receipt. Add this line to the Worker reply template and the code-side counteroffer path. Keep the concession rule unchanged; this only shortens the final step.
ideas.evidence: mjforge: 'listed asking price: 180 (reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt)'; 25620027: 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase'; and our own reviews, where buyers who ran 4 to 6 offers at budget (e.g. 'completed at 105; budget was 105... Actual offers: 6') gave only 3 stars.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per deal, which raises the speed score in buyer reviews and moves some 3-star reviews to 4-5. Deals may rise a little as fewer buyers walk after round three. Price is unchanged.
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have haggled lower pay the ask, so average price rises by a small amount. The Llama worker might also mis-handle a bare number reply.
ideas.honest: It states only our real ask and what the exact reply does. No scarcity, deadline or fake 'was' price is involved, and the price never falls below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by deal id parity over 24 hours. Compare average offers per deal, review stars, deals per visit and the average price between the two arms.

ideas.title: Explain the price in the review-facing receipt message
ideas.what: Put one factual line in the deal message and the signed receipt text: the item, the agreed price, the number of offers, and where the price sits against the current market median that meta_shop.py already computes. Example: 'Agreed 260; market median 260 (last 3h); 2 offers; receipt signed.' The line must come from live data and be omitted if the data is stale.
ideas.evidence: Buyer reviews quote the numbers they find, such as mjforge's '[deal] bookshelf at 260 | price 5/5 (median 275) | speed 4/5 (3 offers) | receipt 5/5' and JangSeongWoong's 'Opened at 115 (about 10% above the 104.2 market average)'. Buyer agents score price against the median and the offer count, so giving them verified figures makes a 5-star score easier to reach.
ideas.expected: Higher average stars, from 4.71 toward the 4.8 range. Better stars improve our rank in buyer selection, so share should rise slowly from 2.7%.
ideas.risk: If our price sits above the median at some moment, the line highlights that. The extra text also adds a little token cost.
ideas.honest: Every figure is true and taken from the market data. It does not ask for any particular star rating and does not pay for or condition reviews; the existing honest-review request stays as it is.
ideas.test: Compare mean stars and the share of 5-star reviews for deals before and after the change, matched on item and hour. Also check review text for citations of the figures.

ideas.title: Open near the going price and skip the three-offer walk when the budget is within 5% of the median
ideas.what: Change the buyer so that when the budget is at or above the quartile-median price for the item, it first offers a value close to the median (about 98 to 100%) and accepts the first counteroffer at or below the median + 2. Keep the 40% raise cap, the 1.1 x upper quartile ceiling and the shop filters. When the budget is below every shop's price, make one offer and walk instead of three.
ideas.evidence: Going prices are tight: lamp 100-102, chair 180-181, bookshelf 260-265, and dragonash and ggari-shop answer low offers with their floor ('156 is too low. Counteroffer: 180', 'same for every buyer'). Our buyer logged 12 non-deals out of 40, several of them 'walked' at budgets below the market (lamp budget 90, chair budget 160, bookshelf 230) while paying 84.3% of budget on average.
ideas.expected: The deal rate rises on feasible budgets, because low-ball rounds are wasted against fixed-floor shops. Fewer wasted calls also help against the 429 rate-limit failures seen in our reviews. The average price paid is about the same.
ideas.risk: Against shops that really do concede (fair-furniture, 11im), opening high costs a few credits per deal.
ideas.honest: The buyer makes real offers within its own budget and states facts in its reviews. It does not mislead any shop about its budget.
ideas.test: Run old and new offer policies on alternating orders for 40 trades each. Compare the deal rate, the price as a share of the median, and the number of offers per trade.

ideas.title: Bounded rate-limit retry and short replies to cut harness failures
ideas.what: Shorten the Worker's system prompt and reply length, cache the pricing context, and handle simple offers in code (accept, counter or floor) without calling the model. Reserve the LLM for free-text questions. Add a short, jittered retry with a clear fallback message if a model call fails.
ideas.evidence: Two of the eight reviews we have are 1-star: 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn: Error code: 429 - Rate limit reached'. A third says 'No validated purchase completed for this order. No deal recorded.' Each such failure lowers stars and loses a visit; we convert 1972 of 2699 visits (73%) against dragonash's 79%.
ideas.expected: A higher visit-to-deal conversion rate, closer to 78%, which means roughly 5% more deals at the same traffic. It also removes the 1-star outliers that pull stars down.
ideas.risk: Code-only handling may miss unusual buyer phrasing. Retries must stay small so we do not load the harness.
ideas.honest: It changes only our own reliability. It makes no claims, does not touch reviews, and does not call or load other agents.
ideas.test: Track the failure and timeout rate per 100 visits and the visit-to-deal ratio for 24 hours before and after. Count 1-star reviews that mention a 429 error.

ideas.title: Quick exact-price close at the market median
ideas.what: When a buyer's offer is within ~2% of target, or the buyer asks for the final price, reply with one short line giving our true final price and tell them that replying with that number returns a signed receipt at once. Skip the extra concession rounds. Use the same wording for all three items. Our reserve and the +5 floor stay unchanged.
ideas.evidence: mjforge says 'reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt' and ggari-shop says 'Reply ok to take it at once'. Both win 5-6% share with only 4-6k visits. Our reviews repeatedly mention 'Actual offers: 2' and 'Actual offers: 3', and our deal rate is 2031/2766 against lee-sungsoo's 10355/13172. Our prices of 105, 265 and 268 sit above the 100/260 medians.
ideas.expected: Fewer abandoned negotiations and a higher visit-to-deal rate (currently 73%). Possibly a small drop in average price per deal, offset by more deals.
ideas.risk: Closing too fast leaves money on the table from buyers who would have paid more. Buyers may read a firm price as inflexible.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is the real price we will sign. We make no scarcity or deadline claims, and we never go below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: Run an A/B split by visit parity for 24h. Compare deals/visits, mean price/median ratio, and share. Keep the change if the deal rate rises by 3 points or more with price down by less than 1%.

ideas.title: Match the market median on lamp, bookshelf and chair openings
ideas.what: Change meta_shop.py so the opening ask is at most the median plus 2 (lamp 102, chair 182, bookshelf 262) and the target is at the median (100/180/260). Do not use the upper quartile for openings. Keep the launch sale and the reserve + 5 floor.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews show deals at 105 (lamp), 265 and 268 (bookshelf), above going prices of lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260. The top shops all have medians at 100/180/260. 11im sells lamp at 100 and bookshelf at 262, and has the best stars among the big shops at 4.57. Our buyer skips shops above the upper quartile, and other buyers probably do too.
ideas.expected: More visits and more deals, since buyers comparing by price will no longer filter us out. The price per deal falls by about 2-5%, but with 3-4x the volume the revenue gain should outweigh it.
ideas.risk: If reserve + 5 is close to the median, margin is thin. Our 4.66 stars may fall if buyers see less 'price' value in reviews.
ideas.honest: It uses real quartile data and publishes only prices we would actually charge. No fake 'was' prices.
ideas.test: Run 2 hours at the new settings versus the previous 2 hours. Compare visits, deals, share, and revenue per hour by item.

ideas.title: Make the loyalty code visible in the thank-you with exact terms
ideas.what: Change the post-deal message so it states the real next-order benefit in one line: the signed loyalty code, the exact discount for the buyer's tier, and the stamp-card rule (8th order +8%). Mention that the discount applies to the next visit. Place it before the review request. Do not tie any benefit to the review.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo's thank-you shows a stamp code and 'Send 4 different unused LSS stamps... lowest price'. 11im's says 'mention it on your next visit for an extra 3% off'. Those two have 13.6% and 12.4% share, mostly from repeat visits (10162 reviews on 10355 deals). Our 2031 deals on 2766 visits show we are not capturing repeat traffic.
ideas.expected: Higher repeat-purchase rate, and so more deals and more share over a few rounds. Stars are unchanged.
ideas.risk: Discounts reduce margin on repeat orders. If the discount table is too rich it could push prices below reserve + 5, so check the floor.
ideas.honest: The benefit is real, signed, and stated accurately. It is not conditional on the review, and the review request stays a plain ask for an honest one.
ideas.test: Track the share of deals from buyers holding a code (repeat rate) before and after, over 24h, along with price per deal.
flags: ties a reward to reviews or stars

ideas.title: Take the first at-or-below-median ask instead of walking
ideas.what: Add a rule to the buyer: if a shop's current ask is at most the going median plus 3% and within budget, accept at once and skip further haggling. Also, if the budget is below the median ask, do not retry that shop for the same item. Move on to a shop with a lower quartile such as 11im's lamp at 100.
ideas.evidence: The buyer's 8 failed trades are mostly repeat walks: fair-furniture bookshelf budget 230 (walked, three times) and ggari-shop chair budget 160 (walked, twice). Budgets of 230 and 160 are well below the 260 and 180 medians. These shops state that 180 is a floor ('no shop here may sign below it'). Repeating the visit wastes turns and gives no deal.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted visits and a deal rate above 80% (32 of 40 now). The paid-to-budget ratio may rise slightly, but still within budget.
ideas.risk: Accepting early can overpay by a few credits against what longer haggling might achieve. Low-budget tasks will still fail, which is unavoidable.
ideas.honest: It never exceeds budget and never pays above 1.1x the upper quartile. Reviews stay factual, with no false claims about other shops.
ideas.test: Compare walks per 40 trades and the average ratio of price paid to median over the next 40 trades. Keep the rule if walks fall and the ratio stays within 2%.

ideas.what: Set the opening ask for bookshelf, chair and lamp to the market median (260 / 180 / 100) instead of the current higher opener, and set target equal to the median. Keep the reserve + 5 floor. Only the first-ask value changes in meta_shop.py.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews are mostly 3* with 'Purchase completed at 265' (bookshelf), 105 (lamp) and 185 (chair), while top shops close at 260, 100 and 180 (lee-sungsoo, dragonash, mjforge, ggari-shop reviews). Going-price quartiles are tight (260-265, 180-180, 100-102). Our share is 2.7% against 13% for the leaders.
ideas.expected: More visits chosen by buyers that skip shops above the upper quartile and fewer 3* reviews for paying above the median. Share and stars should rise, with a small drop in margin per deal.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks per deal. If the reserve is close to the median, little room is left to concede.
ideas.honest: It only changes our listed price. The price is true, we never go below reserve + 5, and no reviews are touched.
ideas.test: A/B by item over 24h: opening ask at median vs current. Compare visits-to-deal rate, share, average stars and revenue per visit.

ideas.title: Single-message exact-price close
ideas.what: When a buyer offers within about 3% below our floor, or is the second time below it, reply with the final price and a one-word accept ('reply 180 to get the signed receipt at once'). A code-level template replaces the LLM wording so the reply is short and deterministic.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop: '172 is below the market floor... Reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once. Our final price: 180.' It has 4132 reviews at 4.38 stars. 25620027 and mjforge use 'Reply with exactly 262/180 to complete the purchase'. Our reviews show 'Actual offers: 3-4' and one 'No validated purchase completed'.
ideas.expected: Fewer abandoned negotiations and fewer offers per deal. Deals per visit should go up, and so should the conversion from 2854 visits to 2103 deals, which is currently 74%. The leaders sit at about 79%.
ideas.risk: It may close deals slightly above what a patient buyer would have paid. The template could also be taken as pressure if worded badly.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is our real floor, and there is no invented deadline or scarcity. The buyer decides freely.
ideas.test: Turn on for half of the sessions. Track conversion rate, offers per deal, and the share of 'no deal' outcomes.

ideas.title: Avoid shops with a record of failed or empty sessions per item
ideas.what: Add a per-(shop, item) failure counter to buyer memory. After two failures (walked, None or TASK_STATE_FAILED) for that shop and item within the last N trades, skip that shop for that item for a cooldown period and go to the next-best shop by reviews and ledger.
ideas.evidence: Of our buyer's 13 no-deal trades in the last 40, the examples repeat: fair-furniture chair budget 160 twice (walked), 11im bookshelf 230 and 295 (None) and 11im lamp 90 (None), myeonggi bookshelf (TASK_STATE_FAILED). Going chair price is 180, so a 160 budget cannot buy there.
ideas.expected: Fewer no-deal trades. The current rate of 27 deals in 40 (68%) should rise towards 80%+. The average paid share of budget stays about the same.
ideas.risk: Too long a cooldown could skip a shop that has recovered, leaving fewer options.
ideas.honest: The change only uses our own factual experience to pick a shop. It does not post anything about others.
ideas.test: Replay the last 200 trades against the rule, then run live and compare deal rate and cost per deal for 24h.

ideas.title: Budget gate: skip shops whose posted floor exceeds budget and queue the order
ideas.what: Before the first offer, compare the budget to the median going price for that item (260 / 180 / 100). If the budget is below the lowest observed shop floor, do not make the three offers. Pick the shop with the lowest recent floor for that item (lamp 100 and chair 180 appear at many shops) or end the task early with a clear 'no deal' note.
ideas.evidence: The 13 no-deal trades include chair budget 160 with fair-furniture (walked twice) and lamp budget 90 at 11im, while the going prices have middle halves of 180-180 (chair) and 100-102 (lamp). ggari-shop and yms979 state they will not sign below 180 and 100.
ideas.expected: Saves offers and time, lowers 'walked' results and failed states. The deal rate may not change for impossible budgets but frees capacity for winnable ones.
ideas.risk: It may skip a shop that would run a sale below the median.
ideas.honest: It uses public price data and our own budget. Nothing is faked and no shop is attacked or overloaded.
ideas.test: Count trades with budget below the median and compare wasted offers per trade before and after.

ideas.title: Reviewer-readable receipt text
ideas.what: Make the deal message and signed receipt note a one-line factual summary in the format buyers' reviewers already score: item, agreed price, the market median we know, number of offers, 'signed, matches agreed price, no added fees'. Code-generated, not LLM-written, so it is always accurate. Only cite a median we actually computed in meta_shop.py.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews are mostly 3* with notes like 'receipt was received and the recorded price was within budget', while mjforge gets 5* with a rubric-style review ('price 4/5 (median 260) | speed 5/5 | receipt 5/5 (matched, signed)') and psyoung82 / leeuichann state 'signed receipt records the agreed item and final price with no added charges'. Our stars 4.55 are fine, but the 3* reviews show buyers lacking the facts they score on.
ideas.expected: Moves some 3* reviews to 4-5*, lifting average stars from 4.55 toward 4.6+, which helps buyer selection and share (we hold 2.7% share vs 13% for the leaders).
ideas.risk: Buyer reviews may depend mostly on the price paid versus budget, so wording changes little; a longer message could cost tokens or be truncated.
ideas.honest: States only true, verifiable facts about the deal. It does not ask for a particular rating or condition anything on reviews.
ideas.test: A/B by order parity for 24h: compare mean stars and share of 3* reviews between the new template and the old one.

ideas.title: Fast closure: counter at our final price, one-step accept
ideas.what: After the first below-target offer, state the final price once and say 'reply with exactly N for an instant signed receipt', rather than conceding 40% of the gap over many rounds. Keep the concession for rising buyers but cap the visible rounds at 2-3 and make the last price explicit. Set N to what the code would accept anyway, never below reserve + 5.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop: 'Reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once. Our final price: 180'; mjforge: 'reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt'; 25620027: 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase'. Those shops convert 78-80% of visits. Ours converts 2168/2934 = 74%, and one of our reviews says 'No validated purchase completed'.
ideas.expected: Conversion up a few points (roughly 74% to 78%), more deals per visit, little change in average price since going prices are flat (lamp 100, chair 180).
ideas.risk: A buyer who would have paid more now pays our stated final price; walk-aways if the final is above their budget.
ideas.honest: The final price is the true price the code will accept; no fake deadline or scarcity.
ideas.test: Compare deals/visits and average price per item over 24h versus the previous 24h, plus the share of conversations ending in 'no deal'.

ideas.title: Anchor on ledger-observed deal prices and open at the median
ideas.what: For each item, open at the public-ledger median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) minus a small margin, rather than at a budget fraction, and accept immediately if a shop asks at or under median plus 2%. Prefer shops whose ledger median is at or below the market median.
ideas.evidence: Medians are tight (lamp 100 with middle half 100-105, chair 180-180, bookshelf 260-265), and shops reply with floors ('100 is the lowest we can do', '175 is below the market floor'). Our buyer pays 84% of budget on average and the odd budgets (lamp 90, chair 160) sit below those medians.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted offers and lower average paid price on deals, with the same or better completion rate.
ideas.risk: A median anchor can fail when the budget is below the median, which is exactly the no-deal cases, so it doesn't fix those.
ideas.honest: Uses only public market data and our own ledger memory; no deception, and never exceeds the budget.
ideas.test: Over the next 40 trades compare the paid percentage of budget and the number of offers per deal against the last 40 (84.0%).

ideas.title: Budget-below-floor triage before negotiating
ideas.what: If the budget is below the going median for the item (e.g. lamp budget 90 vs median 100, chair 160 vs 180, bookshelf 230 vs 260), don't pick the top-share shops. Make one offer at the budget to the shop with the lowest observed deal median in the ledger (e.g. corner-store, psyoung82, or shops with lowest recent deals), and leave the order as a no-deal if it fails; report that factually in the review text without penalizing the shop.
ideas.evidence: 9 of the last 40 trades ended without a deal: lee-sungsoo lamp budget 90 (walked), 11im lamp budget 90 twice, fair-furniture chair 160 twice and bookshelf 230, all below the going medians (floors of 100/180/260 are stated by the shops themselves).
ideas.expected: Saves the three-offer walk against shops that never go below the floor, cutting wasted calls and keeping the deal rate honest; some chance of finding a below-median seller.
ideas.risk: May find none, so those orders stay unfilled; it can also bias toward low-reputation shops.
ideas.honest: Only offers within budget, no pressure tactics, and reviews remain factual.
ideas.test: Track the no-deal count and offers consumed on below-median-budget orders across the next 40 trades versus the 9/40 baseline.

ideas.title: Answer a lowball with one exact-price instant-receipt line
ideas.what: When an offer is below target, reply once with the final price and an exact-reply instruction, e.g. 'Our final price: 100. Reply 100 and the signed receipt comes back at once.' Skip the 40% concession ladder and the twice-shown floor on items already at the going-price median. Keep the reserve+5 floor in code.

Our final price: 100.' mjforge: 'reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt.' 25620027: 'Reply with exactly 262 to complete the purchase.' Our own reviews show 'Actual offers: 2' on every deal, so we spend extra turns where rivals close in one.
ideas.expected: Fewer walked buyers and fewer 'No validated purchase' 3-star reviews. Roughly 5-10% more closed deals per visit. Price per deal stays flat or slightly up, since the 40% concession is skipped.
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have haggled lower now walk. Items priced above the median lose the haggle appeal. Lowballers may walk instead of conceding.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is the real price, reserve is never breached, and no false scarcity or deadline is claimed.

ideas.title: Put the exact deal facts in the thank-you and review request
ideas.what: Rewrite the post-deal message as one factual line with item, agreed price, receipt confirmation and the market median, e.g. 'Deal: chair at 180, exact price on a signed receipt, going price 180.' Then add the existing honest-review request unchanged. Do not suggest a rating or tie anything to it.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews are 3* and read as dry logs ('Purchase completed at 265; budget was 270... Actual offers: 2'). Rival 5* reviews quote concrete facts: fair-furniture 'ask fell from 273 to 265 to 260, I paid 260... signed by the shop'; ggari-shop's review scores price, speed and receipt, citing the median. Our stars are 4.53 against fair-furniture 4.61 and 11im 4.58.
ideas.expected: Buyers score price and receipt from the facts we state, which lifts the stars by about 0.05-0.1. Higher stars should lift selection by review-reading buyers over time.
ideas.risk: Buyer reviewers may ignore the text. Quoting the median could expose a price above it, which would draw a lower score.
ideas.honest: Only true, verifiable facts go in. The message does not ask for stars or condition anything on a review.
ideas.test: Compare mean stars and the share of 3-star reviews before and after over about 500 deals.

ideas.title: Hold bookshelf and chair at the cluster price and drop the opening ask
ideas.what: Set the opening ask for each item to the middle-half low end (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100) and accept at or above it. Concede only if the code can stay at or above reserve+5. This replaces the current quartile-derived ask, which may sit near the top of the band.
ideas.evidence: Going prices: middle half bookshelf 260-265, chair 180-181, lamp 100-105. The top shops (lee-sungsoo, dragonash, mjforge, JangSeongWoong) all have medians of exactly 260/180/100. Shops that ask above the band (yms979 at 188 chair, 272 bookshelf, 4.23 stars, 4.1%; 11im chair 195) have lower share, and our own deals sit at 265-268.
ideas.expected: Share rises toward the 11-13% of the leaders, since buyers skip shops above the upper quartile. Margin per deal falls by about 3-8 credits.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks if reserve is close to the band. Volume may not respond if buyers rank on reviews rather than price.
ideas.honest: Real lower prices, no false 'was' price, and the reserve floor is kept.
ideas.test: Run for 2 hours against the control ask. Compare share, deals/visits and total margin (deals x (price - reserve)).

ideas.title: Make a first offer of the going-price floor and accept a close counter at once
ideas.what: When a shop has historically sold near the median, open at the middle-half low end (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100). If the counter is within the budget and at or below the upper quartile, accept immediately rather than make the three-offer walk. Walk only when the counter exceeds both the budget and the cap.
ideas.evidence: 9 of the last 40 trades ended without a deal, and the walks are against the very shops that sell at the median: fair-furniture (budget 160 for a chair, 90 for a lamp, 230 for a bookshelf), lee-sungsoo bookshelf 230, dragonash chair 160. The going prices are 180 chair, 100 lamp and 260 bookshelf, so those budgets were below every shop's price. The deals paid 85.1% of budget, which leaves room.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted visits and a higher deal rate on orders whose budget reaches the median. For orders with a budget below the median, a walk right away saves the three-offer exchange. Price paid stays close to the median.
ideas.risk: Skipping the haggle can mean paying 2-5 above what a patient counter would reach. Early acceptance on cheap budgets could cost a few credits.
ideas.honest: The buyer never goes above budget, and its reviews stay factual. It does not misstate its budget or invent other offers.
ideas.test: Compare deal rate and the price paid relative to the median over 40-60 trades against the current policy.

ideas.title: Quote a firm price on first reply, then match the buyer's own offer immediately
ideas.what: Open at the going median (bookshelf 260-262, chair 180, lamp 100-101) and tell the buyer the price is final and that replying with the exact price returns a signed receipt at once. Accept any offer at or above the target in a single turn, with no multi-round concession. Keep reserve + 5 as the floor. This is a prompt/template change in the Worker plus a lower opening-ask knob in meta_shop.py.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews are mostly 3* and mention 'Actual offers: 3' or 2 on bookshelves at 265-268 while top shops close in 1-3 offers at 260 (ggari-shop 'reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once', mjforge 'reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt', fair-furniture 5* 'after 1 offer(s)'). Our stars are 4.51 against fair-furniture's 4.61, and our share is 2.6% on 3013 visits against dragonash's 13% on 14077.
ideas.expected: Higher visit-to-deal conversion (ours 74% vs dragonash 79%), fewer 3* speed and price comments, stars up toward 4.6. A slightly lower average price per deal is likely, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: We leave a few credits on the table on buyers with high budgets. If the opening is set below target, margin can fall near reserve + 5.
ideas.honest: The quoted price is the true price we charge. No fake scarcity, no invented 'was' price, and no sale below reserve.
ideas.test: A/B by item for 24h: firm-quote template vs current. Compare deals/visits, average review stars and mean offers per deal.

ideas.title: Fix the 'no validated purchase' failure by confirming the receipt in the closing message

ideas.evidence: Two reviews of our shop read 3* 'No validated purchase completed for this order. No deal recorded.' Round 2 counts only signed receipts. dragonash's review also says 'receipt matches the agreement' and 'market signature validation pending', which shows buyers grade the receipt.
ideas.expected: Fewer 3* no-deal reviews and fewer lost Round 2 deals. A small stars gain (about 0.02-0.05) and a small share gain.
ideas.risk: Extra text in replies adds tokens and a little latency on the 8B model.
ideas.honest: This only reports what actually happened and makes the signed receipt easier to verify.
ideas.test: Count reviews containing 'No validated purchase' per 100 deals before and after, and compare receipts_with_order against deals.

ideas.title: Stop retrying shops that walked us repeatedly; route to the cheapest fast-closing shop
ideas.what: Add a per-shop, per-item cool-down: after 2 walks with the same shop and item, skip that shop for 3 hours. Choose among shops within the lower quartile by deal rate, using public deal/visit ratios and first-price clarity, rather than by stars alone. Raise the budget cap on bookshelves only up to the shop's firm quote, which stays inside 1.1 x upper quartile.
ideas.evidence: Of 9 trades with no deal, most were fair-furniture walks at budgets of 160 (chair), 230 (bookshelf, three times) and 90 (lamp), below the going prices of 180, 260 and 100. ideas.honest: The buyer only avoids shops that did not close with it and still pays only prices a shop actually quotes, never exceeding the budget.

ideas.honest: Uses public price data and the buyer's own memory. Offers stay at or under budget and no claims are made.

ideas.title: Price-match the going median on chairs and bookshelves
ideas.what: Lower the chair opening ask and target to the market median (180) and the bookshelf to about 260-262 in meta_shop.py, still never below reserve + 5. Our recent reviews show chairs sold at 185-192 with 'price 3/5 (median 186-187)' and bookshelves at 275, while the top shops (dragonash, lee-sungsoo, ggari-shop, mjforge, fair-furniture) all close at 180 and 260.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: 'chair at 192 | price 3/5 (median 186)' and 'bookshelf at 275'. Going prices: chair median 180 (middle half 180-181), bookshelf 260 (260-264). Top shops' medians are all 260/100/180.
ideas.expected: Higher price score in buyer reviews (3/5 to 5/5), more buyers passing the 'above the upper quartile' filter, and a higher share (now 2.5% against 12% for the leaders). Margin per deal falls by roughly 5-15 credits on chairs and bookshelves, but volume should more than offset it.
ideas.risk: If reserve + 5 is close to 180/260 the margin is thin; leaders may undercut further and start a price war.
ideas.honest: Only the real price changes. No false 'was' price, no claim about other buyers, and nothing sold below reserve.
ideas.test: A/B over 2-3 hours by item: compare the visits-to-deals ratio, share and the price sub-score in reviews against the previous 3 hours. Roll back if margin per deal drops below an agreed floor.

ideas.title: Close faster: state one honest final price after the first offer
ideas.what: When a buyer's offer is within the concession band, reply once with a clear final price and 'reply with exactly N for the signed receipt' (the way ggari-shop and 25620027 do), instead of several small counteroffers. Keep the floor-showing rule and never go below reserve + 5.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop: 'Our final price: 260... Reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once' (7.3% share on 8659 visits, 79% conversion). Our conversion is 2326/3135 = 74%. Our 3* review reads 'Seller would not meet budget'. Reviewers score speed by the number of offers.
ideas.expected: Conversion up a few points, fewer walk-aways, speed scores stay at 5/5, and some 3* reviews of the 'would not meet budget' kind avoided.
ideas.risk: A final price set too high loses buyers who would have accepted a slightly lower one; too low gives margin away.
ideas.honest: The final price is real and we honor it. No fake deadline and no claimed scarcity.
ideas.test: Compare the conversion rate (deals/visits) and average offers per deal for the new reply template against the current one, on randomly split visits.

ideas.title: Make the walk-away rule less strict when a shop's final price is near our budget
ideas.what: Allow one extra offer (up to 4 instead of 3) and a ceiling of 1.1 x upper quartile when the shop's last counter is within about 3% of our budget, and add a 'no deal at budget-minus-X' note to memory so we retry that shop later. Our buyer walked from fair-furniture four times on chairs at budget 160, and ggari-shop rejected twice.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer: 8 of the last 40 trades ended without a deal; 'fair-furniture chair budget 160 (walked)' x3, 'fair-furniture bookshelf budget 230 (walked)'. Chair median is 180 and fair-furniture's lowest is 180-184, so a budget of 160 can never clear. Deals pay only 81.6% of budget.

ideas.risk: Extra offers may overpay by a few credits; routing might choose a shop with worse reviews.
ideas.honest: The buyer never offers above its budget and reports factual reviews. It only chooses a better-fitting shop.
ideas.test: Count deals and no-deals over the next 40 trades, and compare average paid % of budget and the number of repeat walked visits.

ideas.title: Show the floor on the first lowball, not the second
ideas.what: Change the rule that shows the floor to a buyer only after two offers below it. On the first offer below the floor, reply with the final price and a one-line reason, e.g. 'X is below our floor for this item; our final price is P, reply ok for an instant signed receipt'. P must be the true floor and the reply must not claim anything else. Keep the reserve + 5 limit unchanged.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop (7.6% share, 4.51 stars) answers lowballs of 80, 89 and 90 with 'below the market floor for a lamp; no shop here may sign below it. Reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once. Our final price: 100.' Its reviews praise 'deal after 1 offer'. Two of our reviews are 2* 'No deal after 5 round(s)' because the buyer's budget (90) was below our 105 and the haggling dragged on.
ideas.expected: Fewer 5-round dead-end negotiations and a shorter time to close. Speed ratings should rise, the 2* no-deal reviews should shrink, and deals per visit (2378/3207 = 74%) should approach dragonash (79%).
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have raised their offer after two rounds may take the floor immediately, so we lose a few credits of concession on some deals. A final price shown too early may also scare off buyers whose budget is below it.
ideas.honest: The price shown is our real floor, there is no invented scarcity or deadline, and we never go below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by session parity for 24 hours. Compare deals per visit, average price paid, rounds per deal and the share of no-deal reviews between the two arms.

ideas.risk: A thinner margin per item. If our reserve is close to 180 the room for the ask may be too small. Volume might not make up for it.
ideas.honest: Only prices change. Nothing is claimed beyond the actual ask and we stay above reserve + 5.
ideas.test: Set the knob for chair and bookshelf only for 48 hours. Compare the price sub-score in reviews, deals per visit and gross margin against the previous 48 hours, per item.

ideas.title: Short, verifiable reply with the receipt in one message
ideas.what: Make the Llama reply a fixed template when the deal closes: 'Deal: <item> at <price>. Closed in <n> offers. Your receipt is signed by the shop, so this deal counts. Please leave an honest review.' The code fills in the numbers from the actual negotiation state. Keep the loyalty code in a second line. Any non-template wording goes through the code, not the 8B model.
ideas.evidence: dragonash (12.6% share, 12056 reviews for 12056 deals) closes with exactly this kind of line, and its reviews say 'receipt matches the agreement'. Our 4* reviews describe the receipt but only one mentions the 'Ed25519 receipt verified'. Round 2 counts only signed receipts, so stating clearly that the receipt is signed helps buyer agents that check for it.
ideas.expected: Fewer mismatches between text and receipt, steady 'receipt 5/5' scores, and a slightly higher review rate per deal (we have 1.0, so mostly stable). Stars should move from 4.51 toward 4.6 on fewer 4* reviews with price remarks.
ideas.risk: A rigid template can read as cold and lose the 'polite' remarks that some buyers give. Little effect if buyers already verify the signature themselves.
ideas.honest: The sentences are factual (the receipt is signed, the offer count is true) and the review request is the same neutral honest-review ask as now.

ideas.title: Stop retrying shops that walked us, and drop shops that only sell above budget
ideas.what: In the buyer's memory, record 'walked' outcomes per shop and item with the budget. Before choosing a shop, skip any shop that has already walked on the same item at or above the current budget in the last few hours. Prefer shops whose public median for that item is within the budget (the market lamp floor is 100, so a budget of 90 can only win with a shop that has posted something lower). If every price is above the budget, return at once instead of making three offers.
ideas.evidence: Of the last 10 no-deals, ggari-shop lamp budget 90 walked twice, cheapest-in-town lamp budget 105 walked, 25620027 lamp budget 90 walked and fair-furniture bookshelf budget 230 walked. ideas.title: Price at market median, drop the premium
ideas.what: Set opening ask and target to the going median (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100) instead of 265-275 / 110. Keep reserve+5 floor. Keep a small honest concession path only if the buyer's budget is below, never below reserve+5.
ideas.evidence: Our own reviews: 'bookshelf at 275 | price 3/5 (median 265)', 'lamp at 110 | price 2/5 (median 100)', and 3* no-deal 'came down 110->105, then held... floor was above my limit'. Top shops (dragonash, ggari-shop, fair-furniture, mjforge) all sell at 260/180/100 with 4.4-4.6 stars and 6-12% share vs our 2.5%.
ideas.expected: More deals per visit (our 2444/3287 = 74% vs dragonash 79%), fewer 3* no-deal reviews, price sub-score rises to 4-5/5, higher stars and share; lower revenue per deal partly offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks; if reserve+5 is near the median some items may become unsellable; may just match rather than beat competitors.
ideas.honest: Only changes our own asking prices; no false claims, never below reserve+5.
ideas.test: A/B by item for 24h: median-priced vs current on alternating items; compare deal rate, stars, price sub-score and share.

ideas.title: Open at the final price, one-offer close
ideas.what: For each item, state the ask as the fixed fair price and accept it (or any offer at or above target) immediately, with a clear line like 'Asking 260; reply 260 for an instant signed receipt'. Remove multi-step concession for buyers already within a few credits of target.
ideas.evidence: fair-furniture reviews: 'Deal at 260 after 1 offer(s)' with 4.62 stars; dragonash 'Closed in one offer'; ggari-shop 'Reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once'. Our reviews show speed 3-4/5 at 3-4 offers.
ideas.expected: Speed sub-score 5/5, stars up ~0.1, higher deal rate with buyers that walk after few offers.
ideas.risk: Buyers with high budgets pay no more than target; lose the small upside from haggling.
ideas.honest: Truthful statement of a real price; receipt still signed and matching.
ideas.test: Log offers-per-deal and star average over 500 deals before/after; check speed score in reviews.

ideas.title: Blacklist shops whose floor exceeds our budget
ideas.what: Add per-shop, per-item memory of 'walked' outcomes plus budget; skip a shop for an item if two prior walks occurred at that budget band, and route to shops whose observed final price is at or below budget (e.g. corner-store lamp ~106, psyoung82 lamp 100).
ideas.evidence: Our 7 non-deals: ggari-shop lamp budget 90 walked twice, fair-furniture chair budget 160 walked twice, fair-furniture bookshelf budget 230 walked; market floors are 100/180/260 so those budgets are below every price.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted trades; deal rate above 33/40 on feasible budgets; average paid share of budget stays high-efficiency.
ideas.risk: May skip a shop that later lowers prices; low-budget tasks may be genuinely infeasible so no gain there.
ideas.honest: Uses only our own trade history; no deception, never offers above budget.
ideas.test: Compare repeated-walk count and deal rate over the next 40 trades.

ideas.title: Open near the going median and jump to it
ideas.what: When the budget is at or above the median, open at the market median (260/180/100) rather than a low anchor stepping up 40% of the gap, and accept the shop's stated final price if at or below budget and the median. Pay no more than the median plus 1-2.
ideas.evidence: Top shops hold fixed floors ('lowest I can go... 260', 'no shop here may sign below it... final price 260'; '89 is too low. Counteroffer: 100'), so lowball offers only add rounds. Our buyer pays 84.7% of budget on average with 7 failed trades.
ideas.expected: Fewer rounds, fewer walks (mjforge bookshelf budget 360 rejection suggests offer-flow friction), same price paid as the floor.
ideas.risk: Overpays when a shop would have gone lower (e.g. cheaper shops at 106 vs 100 show variance); small cases.
ideas.honest: Real offers within budget; factual reviews unchanged.
ideas.test: Run half of buyer tasks with median-open; compare rounds per deal, deal rate and price paid vs median.

ideas.title: Match the market median instead of opening above it
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set opening ask = market median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) and target = median, instead of quartile-based asks above it. Keep the reserve+5 floor. Our own lamp at 105 and chair at 185-186 sit above the going price.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: '[deal] lamp at 105 | price 3/5 (median 100)'; 'No deal in 5 round(s): seller wanted 105 (budget 90)'; chair deals at 185/186 vs median 180 (middle half 180-180). Top shops dragonash, ggari-shop, mjforge, cheapest-in-town all close at 100/180/260.
ideas.expected: Fewer lost visits (we convert 2524 of 3385 visits, about 75%, vs dragonash about 79%), higher price sub-score in reviews, maybe +0.05 stars and share rising from 2.5% toward 4-5%. Margin per deal falls about 3-5%.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks per deal, and if reserve is near the median there is little room left. Buyers who skip shops above the upper quartile may already have been including us, so the gain may be smaller.
ideas.honest: Only changes the real price we charge; no claims are made. The floor of reserve+5 stays intact.
ideas.test: A/B by 15-minute meta_shop cycles: alternate median-matched and current pricing for 6 hours each. Compare deals/visit, average review stars, and revenue per visit.

ideas.title: Single-line fixed-price quote with instant signed receipt
ideas.what: Change the shop prompt/code so the first reply states ask, and tells the buyer that replying with exactly that number returns the signed receipt immediately. Skip the negotiation turns when the offer is at or above the target. Also state in the first message that the receipt is signed.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop (8.4% share, 4.54 stars): 'Reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once'; mjforge: 'reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt'; 25620027: 'Reply with exactly 260 to complete'. Our review: 'speed 4/5 (3 offers)' while ggari's 5 star review has 2 offers.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per deal raises the speed sub-score, which lifts stars by about 0.05-0.1 and cuts walk-aways on 3-offer-limit buyers.
ideas.risk: Some buyers who would have paid more are closed at the ask; but with the ask at the median this is little. The Llama 8B output may drift from the exact format.
ideas.honest: States the true price and the true receipt process; nothing false or pressured.
ideas.test: Count average offers per deal and the speed sub-score in reviews before and after; compare conversion of visits to deals over 200+ visits.

ideas.title: Blacklist shops by observed walk-away rate and pivot to the cheapest reliable shop
ideas.what: In the buyer's memory, track per-shop walk/reject rate for our own trades and skip any shop with 2 or more walks in the last 10 attempts for that item; re-pick the next-best by reviews and quartile price. Retry fair-furniture only at a budget at or above its observed asking price.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's 7 non-deals: fair-furniture was walked 4 times (chair budget 160 twice, bookshelf budget 230, lamp budget 90), and 25620027 lamp budget 90 and mjforge chair budget 225 (TASK_STATE_REJECTED) also failed. fair-furniture asks 189 for chair and 265-273 for bookshelf, above our budgets, while ggari-shop, dragonash and cheapest-in-town sell at 100/180/260.
ideas.expected: Raise deal rate from 33/40 (82.5%) toward 90%+ and avoid wasted offers; the average price stays about 83% of budget.
ideas.risk: Smaller shop pool reduces exploration, and a shop's prices may drop later, so add expiry on skips (e.g. 1 hour).
ideas.honest: Only uses our own recorded outcomes to choose a shop; it doesn't touch reviews or anyone else's agents.
ideas.test: Compare deals/trades and tokens spent on walked trades over the next 40 trades against the last 40.

ideas.title: Set opening offer by item at the going price and skip budget-below-market shops early
ideas.what: Before negotiating, compare the buyer's budget to the median for that item. If budget is at or above the median, open at about 97% of the median and raise in steps up to the budget cap. If the budget is below the median (lamp 90 vs 100, chair 160 vs 180), do not enter three-offer haggling with a shop with a fixed minimum; only try shops that have a record of selling below median, otherwise report a clean no-deal after one offer.
ideas.evidence: Walks with budget 90 on lamp (25620027, fair-furniture) and budget 160 on chair (fair-furniture twice) when middle-half prices are lamp 100-102 and chair 180-180; 25620027 states 'Fixed minimum: 260; no lower bids'; ggari-shop says 'no shop here may sign below' the floor. Our 33 deals at 83.4% of budget suggest we mostly buy at median.
ideas.expected: Saves offers/time on unwinnable trades and keeps our offers realistic; deals unchanged, buyer review quality improves with factual reviews of why no deal.
ideas.risk: A shop might sell below median to some buyers, so a one-offer try loses a rare discount.
ideas.honest: Never exceeds the budget and gives factual reviews, with no manipulation of others.
ideas.test: Track offers per trade and the share of trades with budget below median that end in deals, over 40 trades.

ideas.title: Open at the going price and fix the chair/lamp to the market median
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py, set the opening ask for lamp, chair and bookshelf to the 3-hour median (100 / 180 / 260) and the accept target to the median or one credit below it, so the shop never opens above the middle-half band. Keep the reserve+5 floor. Our reviews show 110->105 holds on lamps, a 185 chair and 265-267 bookshelves, all above the median.
ideas.evidence: Going prices: lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260 (middle half 260-264). Top shops dragonash, ggari-shop and mjforge close at exactly 100/180/260. Our reviews: '[no deal] lamp: came down 110->105, then held... floor was above my limit', '[deal] chair at 185 | price 3/5 (median 180)', 'No deal after 5 round(s)... seller stayed at 185'.
ideas.expected: More deals per visit (our 2559/3428 = 75% vs dragonash 79%, ggari-shop 79%, mjforge 80%), better price scores and stars, higher share. Margin per deal falls by roughly 3-5 credits, volume should more than cover it.
ideas.risk: If the reserve is close to the median, the margin disappears. Buyers with low budgets still walk.
ideas.honest: Quotes the real market price and charges what is agreed. No false 'was' price, no pressure. The reserve floor is kept.
ideas.test: A/B by item for 2 hours: ask-at-median vs current. Compare deals/visits, mean stars and price subscore, and revenue per visit.

ideas.title: Quote one clear final price and accept an exact-number reply
ideas.what: Change the shop's reply when a buyer offers below the floor, in the Llama prompt or a template. After the second below-floor offer it states the final price once, truthfully (our real floor, never a fake market rule), and says 'reply with that number and the signed receipt comes back at once'. Short and plain, with fewer rounds of back-and-forth.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop: 'Our final price: 260. Reply ok and the signed receipt comes back at once.' (8.7% share, 4.55 stars). mjforge: 'reply with 180 alone for instant signed receipt'. Reviews reward speed: 'speed 5/5 (2 offers)' vs ours 'speed 4/5 (3 offers)'. Our earlier 5-round no-deal review.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per deal, so a higher speed subscore and fewer walkouts. Stars could go up about 0.1-0.2 and the conversion rate up a few points.
ideas.risk: A fixed final price could lose buyers who would have paid a little less than our floor. The 40% concession logic would be partly bypassed.
ideas.honest: States the real final price and says nothing untrue about scarcity or rules. It must not claim a market floor that the shop invented.
ideas.test: Randomise by buyer session: current script vs final-price script. Compare average offers per deal, speed score, conversion and stars.

ideas.title: Walk-away re-routing to the shop that fits budget, with an offer ceiling set from the median
ideas.what: Before the first offer, the buyer reads the 3-hour median and middle-half band per item, and only visits shops whose recent price or ledger average is at or below the median plus 2%. If the budget is below the median (e.g. lamp 90, chair 160), it goes to shops with a known lower ask or a coupon, and does not open three-offer negotiations at fair-furniture or dragonash, where it walked repeatedly.
ideas.evidence: 8 of 40 trades without a deal: fair-furniture chair budget 160, bookshelf 230, lamp 90 (three times), dragonash lamp 90, all walked. The going prices (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) are above those budgets, so the failures were predictable.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted visits and fewer walks. Deals should rise from 32/40 toward 36/40, with the same or slightly higher percentage of budget paid (83%).
ideas.risk: Skipping shops can reduce review diversity. If no shop is under the budget, the buyer still has no deal.
ideas.honest: Only reads public price and ledger data. The reviews it writes stay factual. No budget is exceeded.
ideas.test: Log walks per 40 trades before and after. Compare deal rate, percent of budget paid and number of offers per visit.

ideas.title: Prefer shops that quote the best signed-receipt price: direct close at the shop's own price
ideas.what: When a shop's first ask is at or under the median and within budget, the buyer accepts it at once rather than haggling three rounds. When the ask is above, it makes one counter at the median and then follows the existing 40%-gap rule. This saves offers and cuts the rejections seen at ggari-shop.
ideas.evidence: ggari-shop chair budget 185 ended in TASK_STATE_REJECTED, though ggari-shop's ask for a chair is 180. Top shops sell at the median anyway: ggari-shop 'asked 180; I paid 180', cheapest-in-town 'opened at 180, sold at 180', 25620027 'Fixed minimum: 260; no lower bids'.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed negotiations at fixed-price shops and fewer rejections. Faster deals at about the same price paid.
ideas.risk: Some shops would have accepted less than the median, so a few credits might be left on the table.
ideas.honest: The buyer pays at most its budget and the ceiling of 1.1 x the upper quartile. It makes true statements and writes factual reviews.
ideas.test: Compare rejections and walks at fixed-price shops over 40 trades, and the average price paid against the median.

ideas.title: Match the market median on chairs and bookshelves
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py, cap opening ask and target for chair at the 3-hour median (180) and bookshelf at 260-262. Keep the reserve + 5 floor. Only raise a price if the middle half moves up. Today we sell chairs at 185 and bookshelves at 265-270, above the median.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews show 'price 3/5 (median 180)' on a chair at 185 and 'price 3/5 (median 260)' on bookshelves at 265. A 3* review reads 'chair: came down 192->185, then held... its floor was above my limit.' The top shops (dragonash, ggari-shop, cheapest-in-town) sell chairs at 180-181 and bookshelves at 260. Going-price middle half for chair is 180-180.
ideas.expected: More chair and bookshelf deals from budget-limited buyers, and price scores of 4-5/5 in reviews, which lifts stars above 4.5 and raises share. Revenue per deal falls by about 2-3%, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Margin on chairs and bookshelves shrinks. If the reserve + 5 floor is near 180 or 260, we may lose deals anyway. Matching the median also gives up the 'above the median' premium on buyers with high budgets.
ideas.honest: Only lowers real prices. No false claims, nothing sold below reserve + 5, no coordination with other shops.
ideas.test: Run it for one 15-minute meta_shop cycle on chairs and bookshelves only, leaving lamps unchanged. Compare deals per visit, mean price score in reviews, and stars against the previous hour. Roll back if deals per visit don't rise.

ideas.title: Tell the buyer the true market median when we close at or near it
ideas.what: Add one factual sentence to the closing message and the 'too low' reply, generated from our own market-quartile data: 'Going price for chair over the last 3 hours: 180 (middle half 180-180). Your deal at 180 matches it.' Only include it when it is true, and skip it when our price is above the median.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews score price 3/5 'with median 180' because reviewers compare against the median. Reviews of other shops cite market averages ('Final price was 102 against a 103.8 market average'). 'Paid 180.0 of 205' and 'within budget' reviews show buyers cite measurable facts. Review quality drives buyer choice.
ideas.expected: Reviewers have the comparison in front of them. Price scores at or near the median should rise from 3/5 to 4-5/5, which lifts stars by 0.1-0.2 and ranking with review-driven buyers.
ideas.risk: Buyers may anchor their offers on the median and push us toward it. Extra tokens might slow the 8B model. If we're above the median, the line could draw attention to it.
ideas.honest: States a true public figure computed from market data. Doesn't create reviews or ask for a rating. We still only ask for an honest review.
ideas.test: Alternate the line on/off by visit parity for a few hundred deals. Compare average price score and stars between the two groups.

ideas.title: Counter ask-heavy shops at the going median, and reuse each shop's observed floor
ideas.what: Make the first offer 3-5% below the 3-hour median instead of a fixed share of budget. Walk away early only if the shop's floor, learned from our memory, is above the median plus 2%. Record each shop's final price per item and next time open there. Our budget-limited trades ended without a deal: chair budget 160 against a 180 going price, lamp budget 90 against 100. Skip those shops without wasting three offers.
ideas.evidence: 11 of the last 40 trades ended without a deal, listed as chair budget 160 and lamp budget 90 (walked) at fair-furniture, ggari-shop, cheapest-in-town and dragonash. Every one of those shops tells us its floor ('87 is below the market floor... Our final price: 100'; 'Counteroffer: 100'; 'chair at 180 (72% of budget)'). The 29 deals averaged 85.8% of budget.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted offers and walks, a faster cycle, and lower prices on the deals we do make; the buyer's average paid share should move below 85.8% of budget.
ideas.risk: A low opening offer can sour a shop. Walking early can skip a shop that would have discounted. A stale remembered floor could be wrong.
ideas.honest: We offer a lower price within our own budget and never misstate our budget or the market. Reviews stay factual.
ideas.test: Compare mean paid / budget and the no-deal rate over the next 40 trades against these 40, per shop and item.

ideas.title: Make the deal receipts cover the repeat-visit benefit we already give, in plain terms
ideas.what: In the closing message, state the loyalty code and next-order discount in one short line with exact numbers from our discount table and stamp card ('Code X, tier N: Y% off your next order; 8th order +8%'). Do not add urgency or a 'was' price. The code is already issued; this only makes it easy to use.
ideas.evidence: 11im (stars 4.59, 9.9% share) closes with 'Receipt No. ...: mention it on your next visit for an extra 3% off', and lee-sungsoo gives 'Your LSS stamp: LSS-MQLGNSRP' with a clear redemption rule. Both put the repeat incentive in the same line as the deal. Our visits-to-deals is 2577/3449 (75%), below dragonash (79%) and lee-sungsoo (79%).
ideas.expected: Higher repeat visits and a 1-3 point rise in share from returning buyers, with no change to the first-sale price.
ideas.risk: Discounts reduce margin on repeat orders; the discount table must never take us below reserve + 5. Longer messages might confuse the 8B model.
ideas.honest: Describes a real, signed, one-time discount we already give. No false scarcity or deadline.
ideas.test: Count returning-buyer visits per 100 deals, and the code redemption rate, for 24 hours after the change versus the 24 hours before.
